regions.name: Middle East
overview: US–Iran tit-for-tat escalated again and spread beyond Hormuz. Iran attacked US facilities in Bahrain on 13, 15 and 17 November; the IRGC said it fired six drones at a US radar at Riffa on 15 November, and US officials said all three attempts were intercepted. A US jet struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm on 17 November, and Iran answered on 18 November with drones at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, its first attack on Kuwait in more than two months. Kuwait said it intercepted them. Shipping attacks are near-daily: an ADNOC vessel was hit in the strait on 17 November (1 missing, 11 injured), and another tanker was hit north of Khasab on 18 November. Trump called the June MoU 'a waste of time' and sent a third aircraft carrier, while saying new strikes were 'highly unlikely'. Qatari mediation has stalled.

Yemen's war has turned against the Saudi-backed side in the south-west. On 15 November, government-aligned forces withdrew from Dhubab and the Bab al-Mandeb area to defend Aden, leaving the Houthis in control of the strait. Reports put Houthi forces at Tor al-Baha, roughly 60–80 km from Aden. The coalition replied on 17 November with strikes on 60 targets in Sanaa, Amran, Saada and Hodeidah, which the Houthis say killed at least 17. Houthi missiles at Riyadh continued on 15, 18 and 19 November; debris from the 19 November interception caused material damage. Egypt confirmed that its troops, armour, air defences and surface-to-surface missiles are in Saudi Arabia, and Reuters reports Riyadh is preparing for the war to run into 2027.

Gaza's ceasefire is eroding further. Israel announced its first publicly declared ground operation since October 2025 on 18 November, west of the Yellow Line in central Gaza (Salah al-Din Street, east of Nuseirat and north of Bureij). Earlier, an air strike on Nasser Hospital killed six people on 12 November, and the Hamas Rafah Brigade commander was killed on 14 November. The post-ceasefire toll has reached 1,658. In the West Bank, settlers shot dead a 72-year-old woman near Jericho on 17 November. Eisenkot (deadline 6 December) is holding unity talks with Likud and has opened the door to the Haredi parties. Defence Minister Katz said Israel will stay in Lebanon, Gaza and Syria indefinitely.

Low-intensity pressure persists elsewhere. Israel struck a Hezbollah-bound arms shipment at Janta in the Bekaa on 16 November and hit Qantara on 18 November. Syria saw a car bomb in Jaramana on 14 November (two killed) and continued Israeli raids and detentions in Quneitra. In Iraq, drones hit Iranian Kurdish opposition bases in Sulaymaniyah on 17 November, and a government–Kataib Hezbollah standoff at Jurf al-Sakhar is the first real test of militia disarmament; the IRGC's Qaani flew in to mediate. Jordan's court sentenced the Karak church attackers to death. No armed violence was found in Libya, Egypt or Tunisia.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 12 Nov — Khan Younis (Nasser Hospital): An Israeli air strike on the hospital killed six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, according to the Health Ministry; the IDF said it targeted the Hamas Khan Younis brigade commander. Israeli fire killed 11 people across Gaza that day.
14 Nov — al-Mawasi (Khan Younis): An Israeli air strike killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, as confirmed by the IDF, Shin Bet and Hamas; others were wounded.
17 Nov — Gaza Strip: Israeli fire killed six Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, according to the civil defence agency and hospitals cited by AFP.

18 Nov — Central Gaza (Salah al-Din Street, east of Nuseirat / north of Bureij): Israel launched its first publicly announced ground operation since the October 2025 ceasefire, west of the Yellow Line, citing Hamas violations. Attacks in al-Mughraqa, Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City killed at least four people, and the Health Ministry's post-ceasefire toll reached 1,658.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israeli fire kills several people a day, and on 12 November 11 were killed, including six in a strike on Nasser Hospital. Israel is also targeting senior Hamas commanders, killing the Rafah Brigade commander on 14 November. On 18 November it launched its first publicly announced ground operation west of the Yellow Line since the ceasefire, which signals a shift from containment to manoeuvre. The post-ceasefire toll rose from about 1,602 to 1,658 in two weeks, keeping the 1,800 threshold of the open forecast on a likely track. Katz says Israel will remain in Gaza indefinitely until armed groups are dismantled, and coalition talks in Israel are unlikely to change Gaza policy before mid-December. Over the next 90 days, expect continued lethal strikes, further raids and land seizure west of the Yellow Line, crossings used as leverage, and a severe winter shelter crisis. A full collapse into large-scale offensive operations is a realistic possibility if Hamas retaliates for the killing of its commanders.

events.place: Central Gaza (Salah al-Din Street, east of Nuseirat / north of Bureij)

forecasts.statement: The Gaza Ministry of Health reports that 1,800 or more Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if a Gaza Health Ministry figure, as reported by Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP or OCHA, published on or before 2027-01-31, gives a post-ceasefire death toll of at least 1,800.

forecasts.statement: Israeli strikes or fire kill 25 or more Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on a single day.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Gaza Health Ministry or civil defence, as reported by Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera or OCHA, reports at least 25 people killed by Israeli attacks within one calendar day (or one 24-hour reporting period) between 2026-11-19 and 2027-02-19.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 15 Nov — Southern Lebanon: The IDF said it demolished a Hezbollah tunnel in the south.
16 Nov — Janta (Bekaa, Syria–Lebanon border): The Israeli military said it struck overnight a weapons shipment moving from Syria to Hezbollah; no casualty figures were reported.

18 Nov — Qantara (Marjayoun district): An Israeli air strike hit the town, according to Al Jazeera; no casualties were reported. The same day, Defence Minister Katz said Israel will keep occupying parts of Lebanon until armed groups are dismantled.
18 Nov — Washington: The US Treasury sanctioned Hezbollah-linked targets, including a charity and a gold and cash smuggling network.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel still occupies a security zone in the south and strikes, demolishes and shells there several times a week. The Janta strike on 16 November shows it will also act deep in the Bekaa against supply lines from Syria. No deaths were confirmed this week, but the underlying conditions are unchanged: Katz has openly declared an indefinite occupation, Hezbollah vows resistance, and disarmament under the June framework lags. Over the next 90 days, the main escalation driver is the US–Iran confrontation, which re-escalated this week with Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait. If Washington or Israel resumes large-scale strikes on Iran, Hezbollah involvement and an Israeli air campaign on the Dahiyeh and the Bekaa become likely. Without that trigger, expect continued targeted strikes, interdiction of arms convoys, US financial sanctions, and a growing security gap as UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 December. A strike on the Dahiyeh remains unlikely, as in the open forecast.

forecasts.statement: Israel carries out an air strike on Beirut's southern suburbs (Dahiyeh).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera or L'Orient Today report an Israeli air or drone strike hitting Beirut's southern suburbs between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 13–17 Nov — Bahrain: Iran attacked US facilities in Bahrain three times in five days, citing US drone surveillance and an attack on Iranian communications towers. The IRGC said it fired six drones at a US radar at the Riffa helicopter base on 15 Nov and targeted a US radar at Isa Air Base on 17 Nov; US officials said all attacks were intercepted, and CENTCOM said no US personnel were injured.

17 Nov — Qeshm Island: A US fighter jet struck an IRGC missile launch site in what US officials called self-defence in response to the Bahrain radar attack; an Iranian regional official said there was no serious damage.

15–18 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: UKMTO reported near-daily tanker attacks. A tanker was hit approaching the strait on 15 Nov and another was hit in the engine room on 16 Nov. An ADNOC vessel was struck on 17 Nov (one crew member missing, 11 injured), and a tanker was hit north of Khasab on 18 Nov (crew safe). The IRGC claimed several tankers hit mines and that a VLCC sank (unverified).

18 Nov — Ali Al Salem Air Base (Kuwait): Iran's army said its drones hit US Patriot systems and drone and missile launch platforms; Kuwait said its air defences intercepted the drones, and its Foreign Ministry condemned a 'dangerous escalation'. It was the first attack on Kuwait in more than two months.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Iran is under recurring US strikes on its territory, most recently on Qeshm on 17 November. It has now widened its retaliation from shipping to direct drone attacks on US bases in Bahrain (three in five days) and Kuwait, in what analysts describe as deliberate, calibrated escalation. Tanker attacks around Hormuz continue near-daily under the US naval blockade. Diplomacy is stalled: Trump called the June MoU 'a waste of time', and Qatari mediation has produced nothing, although Trump says talks continue and that Tehran wants a deal. Washington has sent a third aircraft carrier, and CENTCOM's chief met Israel's chief of staff and the Mossad head on 18 November amid reported US–Israeli debate on restarting larger operations. Over the next 90 days, the most likely path is continued tit-for-tat at Hormuz and across the Gulf, with a growing risk that an Iranian attack causes US casualties and triggers a wider campaign. A US and/or Israeli strike on inland Iran remains a realistic possibility, and a Hormuz reopening agreement remains unlikely before February.

forecasts.statement: The United States and/or Israel strike targets on the Iranian mainland away from the Hormuz coast and islands (e.g. Tehran, Isfahan, Natanz, Fordow, or other inland sites).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report a US or Israeli strike on a site in an inland Iranian province (not Hormozgan, Bushehr coast or the Gulf islands) between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: The United States and Iran publicly announce an agreement or framework to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if both governments, or the mediating state (Qatar/Oman) with both sides confirming, announce an agreed arrangement for reopening Hormuz, as reported by Reuters or AP, by 2027-01-31.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 15 Nov — Dhubab / Bab al-Mandeb (Taiz governorate): Government-aligned forces, including the Southern Armed Forces, withdrew from Dhubab airport and the surrounding area to reinforce Aden, leaving the Houthis in control of the strait's Yemeni coast. Reports put Houthi forces at Tor al-Baha, about 60–80 km from Aden.

17 Nov — Sanaa / Amran / Saada / Hodeidah: The Saudi-led coalition said it struck 60 military targets, including missile tunnels and drone workshops. Houthi health officials said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 in a strike on a sponge factory in Hodeidah and two in Kitaf (Saada).

17 Nov (reported) — Marib: Houthi shelling of a displaced persons camp reportedly killed two children and injured 15; government forces said they carried out four air strikes on Houthi positions and missile launchers in Marib.

15 Nov — Taiz / Lahj / Marib / al-Jawf: Government spokesman al-Nuzaili claimed 321 Houthi leaders were killed or wounded in 723 targeted operations under 'Operation Dawn of Yemen' (unverified); the Houthis fired missiles and drones toward Riyadh, the Eastern Province and Mecca under a 'siege for siege' principle.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The war has shifted against the government in the south-west. The withdrawal from Dhubab on 15 November handed the Houthis the Yemeni shore of Bab al-Mandeb, and Houthi units are reported 60–80 km from Aden. Taiz remains encircled. The coalition is answering with heavier air strikes, including 60 targets on 17 November with at least 17 reported dead, while Houthi missile fire at Saudi cities continues almost daily. Saudi Arabia is reportedly planning for the war to last into 2027, and Egyptian and Syrian contingents are now in the kingdom. Over the next 90 days, expect intense fighting on the Aden–Taiz–Bab al-Mandeb triangle and in Marib, more strikes on Houthi ports, fuel and missile infrastructure, mass-casualty incidents with disputed attribution, and worsening displacement. Houthi control of the strait raises the risk to Red Sea shipping, particularly if US–Iran fighting escalates. Breaking the Taiz siege looks even less likely than last week.

forecasts.statement: Yemeni government forces open a land route into Taiz city, breaking the Houthi siege.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera or OCHA report that government forces have reopened a road into Taiz city allowing civilian or aid traffic, by 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: The Houthis attack (with a missile, drone, uncrewed boat or boarding) a commercial vessel in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb or Gulf of Aden.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if UKMTO, JMIC, Reuters or AP report an attack on a merchant ship in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb or Gulf of Aden that is claimed by the Houthis or attributed to them by UKMTO/JMIC or a Western government, between 2026-11-19 and 2027-02-19.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 17 Nov — al-Duyuk al-Tahta (near Jericho, West Bank): Settlers shot dead a 72-year-old Palestinian woman in front of her home near a newly established outpost; Wafa reported 10 others wounded. The IDF said there were Israeli and Palestinian casualties.
14 Nov — Sa'ir (south of Hebron, West Bank): Dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, injuring at least five according to WAFA; the IDF condemned the attackers.

15 Nov — Tel Aviv / Herzliya: Yashar and Likud teams opened unity-government talks under Eisenkot's mandate (deadline 6 December); a Haaretz photojournalist said he was beaten by right-wing activists at a protest outside Eisenkot's home.

18 Nov — Tel Aviv: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper met IDF Chief of Staff Zamir and Mossad Director Gofman, amid reported US–Israeli debate on whether to restart larger military action against Iran.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No missile, drone or rocket attacks on Israeli territory were found this week, so CRITICAL does not apply. The situation is serious, however. West Bank settler violence produced another killing on 17 November, and ACLED says 2026 is on track to be the worst year on record. Israel has also escalated in Gaza with a declared ground operation. The escalation risk is rising: Iran is now hitting US bases in the Gulf, US and Israeli commanders are meeting on possible renewed operations, and a resumed campaign against Iran would very likely bring Iranian missile fire and possibly Hezbollah and Houthi attacks, which would move Israel to CRITICAL. Politically, Eisenkot has until 6 December, extendable by 14 days. He is negotiating with Likud on unity and has opened the door to the Haredi parties after ruling out the Arab-led parties, so a stable coalition remains uncertain. Expect continued West Bank raids and settler attacks, isolated Palestinian attacks, and intense coalition manoeuvring.

forecasts.statement: A new Israeli government headed by Gadi Eisenkot wins a Knesset confidence vote and is sworn in.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Times of Israel, Haaretz, Reuters or AP report that the Knesset approved a government with Eisenkot as prime minister by 2027-01-15.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 17 Nov — Sulaymaniyah: Two explosives-laden drones attacked bases of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, according to Reuters; no casualties were reported. Iran has repeatedly struck such bases.

16–17 Nov — Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil province): PM Ali al-Zaidi said security forces would enter the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold over an alleged oil-smuggling network. Kataib Hezbollah vowed to fight if they do, and al-Zaidi dismissed nine Babil security and administrative officials, including the police chief.
16 Nov — Baghdad: IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani reportedly arrived to mediate between Kataib Hezbollah and the government.
17 Nov — Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline: Iraq resumed oil exports to Turkey at an initial 120,000 barrels per day after the line had been largely idle since 2023.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Cross-border drone strikes on Kurdish opposition sites continue, with Sulaymaniyah hit on 17 November. A suspected drone attack also halted the Khor Mor gas field on 8 November, and ISIS sleeper-cell activity persists around Kirkuk. Above all, the government is confronting Kataib Hezbollah at Jurf al-Sakhar, the first serious test of the plan to disarm Iran-aligned groups by mid-2027, with the militia openly threatening to fight. Qaani's mediation suggests Tehran wants to avoid an intra-Shia clash while it is in confrontation with the US. Over the next 90 days, the most likely outcome is a negotiated, partial entry or symbolic handover at Jurf al-Sakhar rather than a full assault, but armed clashes are possible if the deadline is enforced. Renewed US–Iran war would make militia attacks on US diplomatic sites and Gulf neighbours likely. Expect continued Iranian strikes in the Kurdistan Region and ISIS hit-and-run attacks.

forecasts.statement: A drone or rocket attack targets the US Embassy in Baghdad or the US consulate in Erbil.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Shafaq News or Rudaw report a drone or rocket attack aimed at (including intercepted over) the US Embassy in Baghdad or the US consulate in Erbil between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: Iraqi government security forces deploy inside the town of Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil), the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Shafaq News or Rudaw report that Iraqi army, police or other state forces (excluding PMF units of Kataib Hezbollah itself) have entered and established a presence inside Jurf al-Sakhar town, with or without fighting, by 2027-01-31. A visit by inspection committees alone does not count.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 15 Nov — Riyadh / Eastern Province: Air defences intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the capital, and the coalition reported three drones downed over the Eastern Province.

18 Nov — Riyadh: Air defences intercepted two Houthi cruise missiles fired toward Riyadh, and alerts sounded in three other Saudi cities. The Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid International Airport and a financial centre, and the coalition said it destroyed a Houthi launch platform.
19 Nov — Riyadh: A Houthi missile was intercepted over the capital at about 04:45 after a civil defence alert; coalition spokesman al-Maliki said debris fell and material damage was being assessed.

11 Nov — Saudi Arabia: Egypt's Foreign Minister said Egyptian forces had been in the kingdom for months helping defend 'sensitive' sites; Egypt confirmed troops, armour, anti-aircraft batteries and surface-to-surface missiles. Reuters reported on 18 Nov that Riyadh is preparing for the Yemen war to last into 2027.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained after re-testing. Saudi territory is under direct military attack several times a week. Ballistic and cruise missiles and drones were fired at Riyadh and the Eastern Province on 15, 18 and 19 November, and interception debris caused damage in the capital on 19 November. The kingdom is also an active belligerent, striking 60 targets in Houthi-held Yemen on 17 November. The loss of Bab al-Mandeb to the Houthis and their advance toward Aden weaken Riyadh's position and make a long war more likely; Reuters reports planning into 2027. Egyptian, Syrian, French and UK contributions are thickening its air defences. Over the next 90 days, expect continued salvos on Riyadh and energy sites, periodic debris damage and civilian casualties, flight disruption, and possible cross-border Houthi raids in Jizan and Najran. A single mass-casualty strike remains a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast.

forecasts.statement: A single Houthi missile or drone attack on Saudi territory kills five or more people.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Saudi authorities, Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report at least five deaths from one Houthi attack (including interception debris) on Saudi territory between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 14 Nov — Jaramana (Damascus countryside): An explosive device planted in a car detonated near a battery factory, killing a man and his young daughter and seriously injuring his wife, according to SANA. It was the second deadly bombing in Jaramana in just over three months, and no one claimed it.
15 Nov — Jabata al-Khashab (Quneitra): Israeli forces raided homes and shops and detained two people, according to SANA.

18 Nov — al-Samdaniya al-Sharqiya (Quneitra): Israeli forces entered the village with three military vehicles under reconnaissance aircraft, according to state media; on 17 Nov Damascus demanded international action to halt incursions in Quneitra and Daraa.

11 Nov — Quneitra countryside: Israeli forces expelled olive harvesters from farmland and set agricultural land on fire, according to Syrian media; SOHR counted 35 Israeli incursions and movements in the south between 1 and 7 Nov.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Foreign forces continue to operate on Syrian territory: Israeli troops raid villages, detain residents and burn farmland in Quneitra and western Daraa almost daily, and Katz now says Israel will stay in Syria indefinitely. Suwayda remains outside state control, and the Jaramana car bomb on 14 November, the second deadly bombing there since August, shows a persistent bombing threat around the capital. Syria's troop commitment to Saudi Arabia ties it to the Yemen war, and Israel used Syrian territory as a supply route target at Janta on the Lebanese border. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Israeli incursions and detentions with occasional deaths, further IED and ISIS attacks on government forces and minority areas, and security-service raids from Aleppo to Deir ez-Zor. A security agreement with Israel is unlikely before a new Israeli government is formed.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 9–11 Nov — Cairo: Foreign Minister Abdelatty confirmed that Egyptian forces had deployed to Saudi Arabia months before parliamentary approval and are being reinforced to help defend 'sensitive' sites; Egypt confirmed troops, armour, anti-aircraft batteries and surface-to-surface missiles. Middle East Eye, citing military sources, reported a Rafale squadron and warships moved toward Bab el-Mandeb (unconfirmed).
16 Nov — Tripoli (Libya): PM Dbeibah met Egypt's intelligence chief to discuss security cooperation, according to LANA.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No security incidents on Egyptian soil were found this week. Egypt's exposure is growing but external: it has confirmed a substantial force in Saudi Arabia with a defensive mandate, and naval units are reportedly near Bab el-Mandeb just as the Houthis took control of the strait's Yemeni shore. That raises the risk to Egyptian personnel and to Suez-bound shipping, but neither has been attacked yet. Cairo is also deepening its security role in Libya, with its intelligence chief in Tripoli after the embassy reopened. Over the next 90 days, watch for Houthi attacks on Egyptian forces in Saudi Arabia or on Egyptian naval vessels, Houthi threats to Red Sea and Suez traffic, Sinai security, and pressure on the Rafah crossing from the new Israeli ground operation in Gaza. HIGH would apply if Egyptian forces are directly attacked, the Houthis target Suez traffic, or a significant terrorist attack occurs in Egypt.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 15 Nov — Amman (State Security Court): The court sentenced three men to death by hanging for the 23 Oct Karak church attack (nine killed), convicting them on nine counts of premeditated murder for terrorist purposes.

11 Nov — Amman: Prosecutors charged the ex-convict suspect in the 5 Nov killing of police Corporal Jawad al-Salaytah under the 2006 Anti-Terrorism Law and referred him to the State Security Court; the two attacks have renewed debate on counter-terrorism legislation and on releasing terrorism convicts.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No new attacks were found this week, but two lethal terrorist attacks in two weeks (Karak on 23 October and Amman on 5 November), both carried out by recently released militants, still define the threat. The fast-tracked death sentences and terrorism charges show the state treats this as a live network risk, and retaliation or copycat attacks remain possible. It is not CRITICAL, because there is no sustained armed conflict or loss of territorial control. Over the next 90 days, expect continued raids and arrests, possible changes to release rules for terrorism convicts, steady drug and weapons smuggling from Syria, and possible Jordanian strikes in southern Syria. Iran's widening attacks on US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait raise the risk to US-used bases in Jordan; a direct attack on Jordan would justify CRITICAL. If no new attack occurs by mid-December, MODERATE would be justified.

forecasts.statement: Another attack inside Jordan that authorities describe as terrorist kills at least one person.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Jordanian authorities (Public Security Directorate/Petra), as reported by Reuters, AP, The National or Asharq Al-Awsat, attribute a fatal attack on Jordanian territory to terrorism between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 14 Nov — Tripoli / eastern Libya: AFRICOM commander Gen. Dagvin Anderson met PM Dbeibah and Saddam Haftar separately to discuss military unification, border security, counter-terrorism and the Flintlock 2027 exercise; US adviser Boulos warned spoilers of the 4+4 unification framework of sanctions.
14–16 Nov — Zintan: The House of Representatives accused the GNU of blocking its planned session in Zintan, and UNSMIL expressed regret that the session failed.
16 Nov — Tripoli: Dbeibah met Egypt's intelligence chief on security cooperation; no armed clashes were found in reporting for 12–19 Nov.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed clashes, drone strikes or oil blockades were reported this week (the Libya Security Monitor's 18 November edition lists no security incidents). International engagement is intensifying: AFRICOM is talking to both Dbeibah and Saddam Haftar, US envoy Boulos is threatening spoilers with sanctions, and Egypt is engaging more closely in Tripoli. The failed House of Representatives session in Zintan shows the east–west institutional split is still active. The structural risks are unchanged: more than 30 clashes in Zawiya in 2026, drone attacks on the Zawiya refinery earlier in the year, and an open Haftar succession. Over the next 90 days, watch for renewed militia fighting west of Tripoli, institutional deadlock over the 4+4 track, and disputes over the central bank and oil revenue. Sustained fighting would justify HIGH.

forecasts.statement: Armed clashes between rival groups in Zawiya or Surman kill three or more people in a single episode.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Libya Observer, Libya Security Monitor or UNSMIL report at least three deaths from one episode of armed clashes in Zawiya or Surman between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 23 Oct — Tunis / Jebiniana (Sfax governorate): Rare unrest broke out over recent deaths linked to the police; protesters burned a vehicle and tyres, and police fired tear gas.
17 Oct — Tunis: Thousands joined the largest protest against President Saied in years, over economic hardship and restrictions on political freedoms, with hundreds of police deployed.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No new security incidents were found for 12–19 November; parliament is debating the 2027 budget, and the government says the economy is recovering (2.4% growth in the first half). The underlying tension has not eased. October brought the largest anti-Saied protest in years and clashes over deaths linked to the police, and the jailing of critics continues: journalist Zied el-Heni received a further four years on terrorism charges in late October. The state of emergency runs until 31 December. There is no organised armed violence, so HIGH does not apply, and the protest wave is too recent to justify LOW. Over the next 90 days, expect further economically driven protests, more prosecutions of opposition figures and journalists, and a risk of deadly escalation if security forces use more force. Smuggling along the Libyan border is a secondary risk.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: Diplomacy moved fast but produced nothing binding. On 12 November Witkoff and Kushner briefed Putin in Moscow and met Zelensky the same day at Baldonnel near Dublin. Kushner said Putin had agreed to European participation in the next round, while the Kremlin stayed evasive about it. The large prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi had not taken place by 19 November. Zelensky said on 17 November that Ukraine was ready to deliver 'in the coming weeks' and would hand its exchange proposals to the US at talks in Berlin on 19 November. Putin, Trump and Xi met at APEC in Shenzhen (18–19 November) for the first trilateral at that level, but no Ukraine outcome had been reported at the time of writing. The EU imposed new sanctions on nearly 50 banks and approved its largest single payment to Kyiv (about EUR 8bn).

Both sides struck each other's bridges. On the night of 16–17 November Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges, killing two people in Obolon, and Zaporizhzhia's Preobrazhenskyi bridge was also hit. That same night Ukrainian drones and missiles brought down a road span of the Kerch Bridge to Crimea. Reuters verified video of the span in the strait, Al Jazeera reported two people killed, and rail traffic resumed on one track. Russia's Defence Ministry claimed a war-record 1,336 Ukrainian drones downed overnight into 16 November, about 600 of them near Moscow per the mayor, and Ukraine hit the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Krasnodar Krai on 17–18 November.

Russia's winter campaign against Ukraine's cities and grid continues. Three waves of strikes on Odesa's UNESCO-listed historic centre on 18 November killed four, and Zelensky described follow-up strikes on first responders. Outages hit about 700,000 households in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast after 17 November, and Ukraine's Energy Ministry counts more than 1,000 attacks on energy infrastructure since September. On the ground, ISW (14 November) sees Russian mechanised assaults concentrated on the Kostiantynivka and Dobropillia axes, with only marginal shifts elsewhere. ISW also reports that the Kremlin is asking for a temporary local ceasefire in Kostiantynivka, which it assesses would let Russian forces regroup.

Spillover onto the periphery continues below the threshold of hostilities. On 17 November a Russian Geran-type drone flew over Chișinău, Moldova closed its airspace for about half an hour, and the Russian ambassador was summoned on 18 November. Belarus ordered a snap combat-readiness inspection of its border guard units on 16 November. Aliyev and Pashinyan met in Dublin on 12 November, but the signing of their peace treaty still hinges on Armenia's constitutional referendum, which a 13-party opposition bloc is now organising against. Georgia's party-ban hearings ran through their question stage without a ruling, and pro-European protests in Tbilisi passed day 720.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 16–17 Nov — Kyiv: Russian ballistic missiles struck the Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro; Zelensky said four missiles targeted the Southern and three the Northern bridge. Both bridges were closed, two people were killed in Obolon and critical infrastructure was hit, causing water and heating disruption. In the same attack Zaporizhzhia's Preobrazhenskyi bridge was hit and two people were killed there with 31 injured, Smila was struck by eight ballistic missiles, and about 700,000 households lost power in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast (Kyiv Independent, Euromaidan Press).

18 Nov — Odesa: Russian strikes hit the historic centre in three waves, killing four people, including in the UNESCO-protected zone. Reuters cited at least seven injured and Al Jazeera 13. Zelensky called the attack 'brutal and deliberate' and said follow-up strikes targeted first responders and police already at the scene.

14 Nov — Kostiantynivka–Dobropillia axes (Donetsk Oblast): ISW assessed that recent Russian mechanised assaults and a high tempo of attacks show Moscow prioritising the southern flank of the 'Fortress Belt', and reported that the Kremlin is requesting a temporary local ceasefire in Kostiantynivka that would likely help Russian forces reinforce. Elsewhere, Russian forces advanced northeast of Lyman and east of Sloviansk, while Ukrainian forces advanced south of Novopavlivka.

12 Nov — Dublin (Baldonnel): Zelensky met US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hours after they had briefed Putin in Moscow. Kushner said Putin had agreed to European participation in the next round, and Zelensky called the prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi the largest of the war. On 17 November Zelensky said Ukraine would hand its exchange proposals to the US at a meeting with American and European partners in Berlin on 19 November.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia escalated its target set this week. Ballistic missiles took out Kyiv's two main Dnipro road bridges and a Zaporizhzhia bridge, strikes killed four in central Odesa with reported double-taps on first responders, and post-strike outages reached about 700,000 households in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. Over the next 90 days, expect Russia to keep up mixed ballistic, cruise-missile and jet-drone salvos against power, heating, bridges and rail, partly in retaliation for the Kerch Bridge strike, with heavy glide bombs on front-line towns in Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts. On the ground, Russia's main effort is now the Kostiantynivka–Dobropillia sector, where it uses autumn fog to blunt Ukrainian drones. A local ceasefire in Kostiantynivka that would let Russia regroup is unlikely to be accepted by Kyiv, and full Russian capture of the town before mid-February remains unlikely. On diplomacy, the Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange has not happened yet but is still likely before 20 December, since both sides and Washington are publicly committed and Kyiv has delivered its lists. A next negotiating round with direct European participation is a realistic possibility before mid-January, given Kushner's claim of Putin's consent against Moscow's evasive line. A general or energy ceasefire within 90 days remains unlikely while Moscow ties it to territorial and European-security demands, which the EU rejects. Watch for the outcome of the Berlin meeting, any Shenzhen readout, the timing of the exchange, how long the Kyiv bridges stay closed, and Russian progress in Kostiantynivka.

forecasts.statement: Russian forces take full control of the town of Kostiantynivka (Donetsk Oblast).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if DeepState's map or ISW's assessment shows the whole built-up area of Kostiantynivka under Russian control (a Russian MoD claim alone does not count).

forecasts.statement: A new round of negotiations on ending the war is held in which Russian and Ukrainian delegations both take part (directly or through US-mediated proximity talks) together with an official EU or European-government delegation at the same venue.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or the Kyiv Independent reports that a negotiating session took place with Russian, Ukrainian and EU (or named European government) delegations present at the same talks by that date. Separate bilateral meetings, such as Europeans meeting only Ukraine or the US, do not count.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 16–17 Nov — Kerch Bridge (Crimea): A Ukrainian drone and missile strike sent the main road arch of the bridge into the Kerch Strait, leaving a gap in the roadway; Reuters verified the video. The parallel rail bridge stayed up and Russia's Transport Ministry said rail traffic resumed on one track. Al Jazeera reported two people killed. Zelensky called it an 'unprecedented' operation in seven stages over several weeks, and Russia's Investigative Committee opened a terrorism case.

16 Nov — Moscow and 15 other regions: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight across 16 regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas, the largest count of the war (unverified). Mayor Sobyanin said about 600 were aimed at Moscow. Local authorities reported one person killed by Ukrainian drones in Belgorod Oblast, and Ukraine's military said it hit an oil depot in Azov (Rostov Oblast).

17–18 Nov — Krasnodar Krai: Ukraine's General Staff said it struck storage tanks at the Ilsky refinery and a processing unit at the Afipsky refinery; Kyiv Post counts this as the eighth attack on Afipsky this year. Russian officials confirmed attacks on two industrial facilities without details, and authorities have urged oil companies to produce more lower-grade gasoline to avert shortages.

18–19 Nov — Shenzhen (China): Putin attended the APEC summit, where China confirmed the first Trump–Xi–Putin trilateral meeting. Kremlin aide Ushakov said Ukraine would likely be discussed, while a White House official said Trump would not raise it. No substantive outcome on Ukraine had been reported at the time of writing.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia is waging an active war and its own territory is under escalating attack. This week Ukraine collapsed a road span of the Kerch Bridge, Russia's main road link to Crimea and its southern front, Moscow faced what Russia called the largest drone raid of the war, and refineries in Krasnodar Krai were hit again, adding to domestic fuel stress. Over the next 90 days, expect Moscow to use the Witkoff–Kushner channel and its first trilateral with Trump and Xi to push for a broad settlement on its terms, including a new European security order and territorial recognition, while rejecting an unconditional ceasefire. The Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange is likely to happen before 20 December as a low-cost goodwill gesture, but it has slipped past the two-to-three-week window TASS first gave. Expect retaliatory Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges and the grid, and more pressure on Black Sea shipping. Expect Ukraine to keep hitting refineries, depots and the Crimea supply routes, with recurring airport closures around Moscow. Full restoration of road traffic across the Kerch Bridge before mid-February is unlikely given the fallen main arch, so Crimea logistics will depend more on rail, ferries and the land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine. The regime's internal grip remains firm. Watch the Shenzhen and Berlin outcomes, the date and size of the exchange, Kerch repair progress, and fuel-market measures.

forecasts.statement: Russia and Ukraine carry out a prisoner exchange in which each side releases at least 500 prisoners of war (in one swap or in stages announced as part of the Abu Dhabi deal).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or the Kyiv Independent reports that at least 500 POWs per side have been exchanged under the agreement by that date, per official Ukrainian or Russian statements.

forecasts.statement: Russia reopens the road section of the Kerch (Crimean) Bridge to general vehicle traffic in at least one direction after the 16–17 November 2026 span collapse.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Russian official channels (Transport Ministry, Grand Service Express or Crimean authorities), as reported by Reuters, AP, the Moscow Times or Meduza, state that ordinary vehicle traffic has resumed across the road bridge by that date. Rail-only traffic, ferries or a temporary pontoon do not count.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 16 Nov — Belarus (location unspecified): Lukashenko ordered an unscheduled combat-readiness inspection of State Border Committee rapid-response units, per Security Council State Secretary Volfovich via Belta. It includes field exercises in which units march and repel simulated attacks by enemy sabotage and reconnaissance groups; the location and duration were not specified.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was another quiet week. The only reported security development was a snap combat-readiness inspection of border-guard rapid-response units, which fits Minsk's pattern of drills near the Polish and Lithuanian borders since September. No armed border incidents, troop build-ups toward Ukraine or new hostilities were reported. Over the next 90 days, expect Belarus to keep offering itself as a venue and facilitator for talks while its prisoner-for-sanctions bargaining with Washington stalls. Envoy Coale's promised return visit, which he said in September could free 'hundreds', is now well overdue. Expect smuggling-balloon friction with Lithuania and Poland in the winter wind season, further readiness inspections and continued repression at home. A rise to HIGH would require direct military coercion of a NATO neighbour, a serious armed border incident or Belarusian forces joining the war.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 17 Nov — Chișinău: Several Russian drones violated Moldovan airspace, President Sandu said, one of them a Shahed/Geran-type drone over the capital that alarmed residents. The Defence Ministry recorded two violations, per Reuters. Airspace was closed from 16:27 local time for about half an hour, and police received reports of loud bangs in Chișinău and Florești. No casualties were reported.

18 Nov — Chișinău: The Foreign Ministry summoned Russian ambassador Oleg Ozerov to protest the airspace violations, which Foreign Minister Popșoi called a 'serious breach of our sovereignty'. Russia rejects Moldova's accusations and says no proof has been given that the drones were Russian.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Incursions have now reached the capital: on 17 November a Geran-type drone flew over Chișinău, a week after two Banderol cruise missiles crossed the south, and the government closed national airspace and summoned the Russian ambassador. The Defence Ministry counted 44 violations in 2026 up to late September alone. There are still no casualties, no officially confirmed impacts this week and no evidence of deliberate targeting, so the HIGH threshold is not met. Over the next 90 days, expect more crossings whenever Russia hits Odesa and Vinnytsia oblasts, more temporary airspace closures and diplomatic protests. A crash or wreckage on Moldovan soil remains a realistic possibility. Expect faster EU-funded air surveillance and counter-drone procurement, and continued Russian hybrid pressure through cyber activity, Gagauzia and Transnistria's winter energy squeeze. A first fatality, damage to critical infrastructure or evidence of deliberate targeting would justify a review toward HIGH.

forecasts.statement: A Russian drone or missile, or identifiable wreckage of one, falls on Moldovan territory (crash or impact, not only an overflight).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Moldova's Defence Ministry or police report a crash, impact or recovered wreckage of a Russian drone or missile on Moldovan territory, as reported by Reuters, AP or Moldovan official channels.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 11–17 Nov — Batumi: The Constitutional Court's hearings on Georgian Dream's petition to ban five opposition parties went through their question stage, which the court chairman said would run until 17 November. On 11 November Chairman Nadaraia removed Coalition for Change leaders Nika Gvaramia and Maia Kopaleishvili from the courtroom. The court has rejected nearly all of some 14 opposition motions; no ruling had been issued, and the legal deadline is 24 June 2027.

14 Nov — Tbilisi: Tbilisi City Court sentenced security officers to five years each for abuse of authority with violence over the May 2024 beating of opposition politician Levan Khabeishvili, after a closed-door trial with undisclosed defendant names (SOVA). Khabeishvili's lawyer says the special-forces chief bears primary responsibility.

15–17 Nov — Tbilisi: Pro-European protests outside parliament reached their 720th consecutive day, with at least 200 people demanding an amnesty for protest prisoners and the repeal of repressive laws (Caucasian Knot). Organisers are preparing a mass rally for the 28 November anniversary.

10–11 Nov — Geneva: At the 68th round of the Geneva International Discussions, the de facto authorities in Sokhumi and Tskhinvali, backed by Russia, again demanded that Tbilisi sign a non-use-of-force agreement. No substantive outcome was reported, and the next round is set for March 2027 (SOVA).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There is no organised political violence. Repression runs through the courts: the party-ban case is in Batumi, and treason and protest cases target opposition figures. The convictions of officers for the 2024 Khabeishvili beating are a rare case of accountability, but they were handed down behind closed doors. Daily protests continue peacefully at a few hundred people. Over the next 90 days, the party-ban ruling remains the key variable. The question stage has ended and the court has rejected nearly every defence motion, so a ruling banning at least one party before mid-February remains a realistic possibility. Because the legal deadline runs to June 2027, the court can take its time. The 28 November anniversary rally is the most likely flashpoint for larger crowds and forceful dispersal. Expect more criminal cases against opposition figures, deeper conflict with the EU, routine detentions along the South Ossetia line and a stalled Geneva format. Banning the main opposition parties combined with mass protests that are violently dispersed would justify HIGH.

forecasts.statement: Georgia's Constitutional Court rules to ban (declare unconstitutional) at least one of the five opposition parties named in the Georgian Dream petition.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Civil.ge, Georgia Today, JAMnews or Reuters reports a Constitutional Court ruling banning at least one of UNM, Coalition for Change, Strong Georgia/Lelo, the Federalists or Gakharia for Georgia by that date.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 12 Nov — Dublin: Pashinyan and Aliyev met on the sidelines of the 9th European Political Community summit and discussed transport links, trade, border delimitation and confidence-building on the basis of the August 2025 Washington Declaration.

17–18 Nov — Yerevan: Speaker Rubinyan said Armenia rejects Baku's demand for a new constitution as a precondition and is 'ready to sign even today'. Pashinyan said guarantees exist for signing and ratification once a new constitution is adopted, and has said the treaty could be signed in 2027–2028.

18 Nov — Yerevan: Strong Armenia faction leader Narek Karapetyan said the opposition would block the referendum if it saw division or a threat to sovereignty. A 13-force opposition bloc, including Strong Armenia, Kocharyan's Armenia Alliance, the ARF and the Republican Party, has formed to reject what it calls the 'Aliyev constitution'. On 11 November the Anti-Corruption Court let prosecutors pursue expanded charges against Narek Karapetyan.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was a quieter week on the streets, with no new deaths or reported clashes. The confrontation is now institutional: a 13-force opposition bloc has formed against the draft constitution, Samvel Karapetyan remains in detention, and the courts are widening cases against the Karapetyan family. The Dublin meeting with Aliyev kept the peace track alive, but signing still hinges on the constitutional referendum, which Civil Contract cannot call without opposition votes. Over the next 90 days, expect more pressure on opposition MPs and more detentions and court extensions, including on Samvel Karapetyan's one-month detention, which expires in early December. Opposition protests are likely to grow but should stay largely non-violent. Moscow will keep amplifying opposition grievances, and TRIPP design work and the handover of border control will continue. Violent street unrest, a deliberate shooting or armed border incidents would warrant a review toward HIGH.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 12 Nov — Dublin: Aliyev met Pashinyan at the European Political Community summit to discuss implementing the Washington Declaration (transport route, trade, delimitation); Baku maintains it will not sign the initialled treaty until Armenia changes its constitution.
16 Nov — Goytepe border detachment (Iranian border): Border guards intercepted a drug-carrying paratrike flying in from Iran and detained its Iranian pilot, per the State Border Service.
17 Nov — Horadiz and Lankaran (Iranian border): Border guards prevented an attempt to smuggle about 50 kg of narcotics and 3,000 psychotropic pills from Iran, per APA.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was another quiet week with thin reporting. There are no hostilities on Azerbaijani territory. Iranian-border incidents this week were smuggling interdictions with no exchange of fire, unlike the armed intruder killed on 2 November. Diplomatically, Baku banks the Dublin meeting while holding its constitutional precondition. The Karimli 'seizure of power' trial was due to open on 13 November, but no reporting on the hearing was found. Over the next 90 days, expect tight control of the Karimli trial and the Meydan TV and Toplum TV cases, with international criticism. Expect recurring smuggling and drone incidents on the Iranian border amid poor relations with Tehran, and a slow peace track that hinges on Armenia's referendum. Violent clashes during protests, or a pattern of armed incidents on the Armenian or Iranian border, would warrant a review toward HIGH.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's war shifted toward West Kordofan. The army and the Joint Force entered Al-Khuwai (13 Nov), took Al-Morkib, Khamasat and Umm Oweisha east of Al-Nahud (14 Nov) and Al-Sa'atat north-east of Abu Zabad (16 Nov), according to Sudans Post and Anadolu. The RSF still holds roughly 85–90% of the state, including Al-Nahud. Civilians are paying the price: drone strikes attributed by local monitors to the army killed at least 15 people at Abu Qalb (15 Nov) and at least 16 displaced people sheltering in a school in Ghubeish (17 Nov), and thousands are fleeing Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad toward Darfur.

Blue Nile remains the most dangerous cross-border front. The toll of the 10 November RSF drone strike on Bani Shako rose to 16, the army said it shot down a long-range drone near Dandaro on 13 November that had crossed from Ethiopia, and it announced major reinforcements to the front on 16 November. In North Darfur, the Joint Force said it repelled an RSF attack on Kornoi on 18 November.

In the central Sahel, the deadliest verified event of the week was in Niger: unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians travelling to Téra's weekly market near Tillim (Tillabéri) on 12 November. In Mali, the army announced strikes near Abeïbara (14 Nov) and south-west of Sévaré (16 Nov), and escorted convoys delivered 1,505 fuel tankers to Bamako in the first half of November. JNIM claimed 20 attacks across Burkina Faso and Mali over 9–16 November, which cannot be verified under the juntas' information controls. In Chad, the Miski militia reported a deadly army drone strike in Tibesti on 17 November.

In Nigeria, bandit violence in Zamfara and attacks in Plateau continued: gunmen killed up to seven worshippers including a governor's aide at a mosque in Kaura Namoda on 15 November, and at least nine people were killed in Zwagal (Mangu LGA, Plateau) the same night. In Borno, Operation Hadin Kai claimed at least 31 ISWAP fighters killed in air strikes at Kerenoa (12 Nov), Monguno and Arinna (16–17 Nov); these tolls are not independently verified.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 14 Nov — 8–10 km north of Abeïbara, Kidal region: The army general staff said FAMa, supported by partners, struck a regrouping point with fighters, vehicles and a fuel depot. Reconnaissance was continuing; no toll was given.
16 Nov — 33 km south-west of Sévaré, Mopti region: The army said it struck a logistics gathering including motorcycles, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. No toll was given.

9–16 Nov — Mopti, Ségou, Kidal, Timbuktu and Kayes regions: JNIM's media wing claimed nine attacks in Mali against the army, allied militias, Dozo hunters and Russian Africa Corps personnel. The claims carry no tolls and cannot be verified.

c. 16 Nov — Bamako: A new escorted convoy of 840 fuel tankers reached the capital, bringing November deliveries to 1,505 tankers under FAMa escort, according to official figures relayed by regional media.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM, the FLA and IS Sahel still hold or contest large areas, the army keeps striking targets around Kidal and Mopti, and JNIM claims a steady tempo of attacks across five regions. The fact that Bamako still depends on large military-escorted tanker convoys shows that the fuel blockade has not been broken. Over the next 90 days FAMa and the Africa Corps will likely continue air and drone strikes in the north and centre while trying to hold Kidal and the routes north. JNIM is likely to keep up IED and ambush attacks on the Mopti–Sévaré axis and pressure on the supply corridors from Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire. With convoys now running in batches of hundreds of trucks, a JNIM attack on a fuel convoy that kills ten or more people remains a realistic possibility. IS Sahel violence around Ménaka is likely to continue. Watch for a large garrison assault, a renewed tightening of the blockade around Bamako, or signs of strain inside the junta.

events.place: 8–10 km north of Abeïbara, Kidal region
33 km south-west of Sévaré, Mopti region
Mopti, Ségou, Kidal, Timbuktu and Kayes regions

forecasts.statement: JNIM attacks a fuel tanker convoy anywhere in Mali in an incident that reportedly kills ten or more people (drivers, escorts or civilians).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI or ACLED reports a single JNIM attack on a fuel convoy in Mali on or before 31 Jan 2027 with a reported toll of at least ten dead.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 12 Nov — Tillim, near Téra, Tillabéri region: Unidentified gunmen ambushed residents travelling to Téra's weekly market, killing at least 37 civilians; one more died of wounds the next day, bringing the reported toll to 38. Some reports attribute the attack to IS Sahel; no group has been officially named.
16–17 Nov — Near Kobagué, Torodi department, Tillabéri: The National Guard said it dismantled a logistics base of armed groups in a night operation and 'neutralised' two people.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Tillim massacre (at least 37 civilians killed on the road to Téra market) follows ISSP's attacks that killed more than 50 soldiers and gendarmes in late September and confirms that large-scale violence in Tillabéri continues regardless of the thin reporting. Over the next 90 days IS Sahel attacks on civilians, convoys and posts in Tillabéri and the Tahoua–Dosso belt are likely to continue, and another single attack in Tillabéri killing 20 or more people is likely. JNIM is likely to keep pressing in the south-west around Torodi and toward Benin, and Boko Haram/ISWAP attacks around Diffa remain likely. The junta's sovereignty disputes with the EU and Chad keep the political climate tense, and another coup attempt or mutiny remains a realistic risk while the army purge continues.

forecasts.statement: A single armed attack in Niger's Tillabéri region kills 20 or more people (civilians, soldiers or both).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI, ACLED or an official Nigerien statement reports, on or before 31 Jan 2027, a single attack in Tillabéri region occurring after 19 Nov 2026 with a reported toll of at least 20 dead (attackers' own losses excluded).

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 9–16 Nov — Bam, Mouhoun, Séno, Gourma, Oudalan, Sanmatenga and Yatenga provinces: JNIM's media wing claimed 11 attacks on army and VDP positions, checkpoints and patrols, including ambushes and IEDs. The claims cannot be independently verified.

Mid-Nov (date not given) — Yabousgou: JNIM claimed it overran a military position, killing seven soldiers, destroying a vehicle and seizing weapons and motorcycles. This rests only on the group's claim.

13 Nov — Oudalan/northern border: Al Jazeera reported escalating battles between JNIM and IS Sahel along the Mali border. IS Sahel claimed more than 400 JNIM fighters killed around Ganadaouri on 9 Oct; i-Sahel counted at least 120 bodies in published images but could not verify them.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM still claims attacks on the army and VDP across a wide arc of provinces from Yatenga and Bam to Gourma, and the JNIM–IS Sahel war in Oudalan has produced the deadliest inter-jihadist battles on record, according to ACLED. The drop in large, mass-casualty attacks since late June reflects operational choices rather than reduced capability. Over the next 90 days the dry season is likely to bring renewed large garrison assaults in the North, Sahel, East and Boucle du Mouhoun regions, and continued sieges of towns such as Djibo. The JNIM–IS Sahel contest along the Mali border is likely to keep producing large clashes. Repression of dissent and suspected collaborators will likely continue. Given the blackout, analysts should rely on group claims, displacement data and rights-group reporting, and treat all tolls with caution.

events.place: Bam, Mouhoun, Séno, Gourma, Oudalan, Sanmatenga and Yatenga provinces

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 17 Nov — Ghubeish, West Kordofan: A drone strike on the Musab Bin Omair school sheltering displaced families killed at least 16 civilians and injured about 10, according to the Kordofan Observatory, which attributed it to the army. The toll is preliminary.

15 Nov — Abu Qalb, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan: A drone strike on a football field killed at least 15 civilians, including four children, according to the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory, which attributed it to the army. The RSF-aligned Tasis alliance gave a toll of nine; Dabanga could not verify the figures.

13–16 Nov — West Kordofan: The army and the Joint Force entered Al-Khuwai (13 Nov), took Al-Morkib, Khamasat and Umm Oweisha about 60 km east of Al-Nahud (14 Nov), and announced the capture of Al-Sa'atat north-east of Abu Zabad (16 Nov). The RSF still holds Al-Nahud and most of the state.

13 Nov — Dandaro, Blue Nile: The army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone that had crossed from Ethiopia. On 16 Nov it announced major reinforcements to the Blue Nile front, and the Kurmuk governor raised the toll of the 10 Nov Bani Shako drone strike to 16.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: full-scale war continues on several fronts. In West Kordofan the army and the Joint Force have opened a sustained push toward Al-Nahud, the RSF's main stronghold in the state and the gateway to the Al-Sadarat road into North Darfur, while drone strikes attributed to the army have killed at least 31 civilians in Abu Qalb and Ghubeish in three days. Whether the army can take Al-Nahud in the next 90 days is a realistic possibility rather than a likely outcome, since the RSF still holds about 85–90% of the state and has retaken ground before. In Blue Nile the RSF–SPLM-N alliance holds Kurmuk, Sali and Maqja and keeps striking civilians with drones, while the army reinforces Ed Damazin and Roseires; a full army recapture of Sali remains unlikely in this period. The army's claim that drones are crossing from Ethiopia keeps the cross-border risk high. In North Darfur, RSF attacks on Joint Force positions around Kornoi are likely to continue. The RSF's drone campaign against power, water and fuel infrastructure is likely to continue, deepening famine conditions. With continuing foreign arms flows and no credible talks, a truce is unlikely. Expect more displacement toward Darfur, Chad, South Sudan and Ethiopia.

events.place: Abu Qalb, Abu Zabad locality, West Kordofan

forecasts.statement: The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces retake the Sali military base in Blue Nile from the RSF–SPLM-N alliance.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Sudan Tribune, Dabanga, Sudans Post, Reuters or AP reports, on or before 12 Feb 2027, that SAF or allied forces have regained control of Sali (an SAF claim corroborated by footage or a second independent source counts).

forecasts.statement: The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces (including the Joint Force) take control of the town of Al-Nahud in West Kordofan from the RSF.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Sudan Tribune, Sudans Post, Dabanga, Reuters or AP reports, on or before 19 Feb 2027, that SAF or allied forces control Al-Nahud town (an SAF claim corroborated by footage or a second independent source counts).

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 17 Nov — Miski, Tibesti: The Miski Self-Defence Committee said a drone strike it attributed to the government killed at least one civilian. The government did not respond to AFP; Miski remains under the committee's control.

Since 7 Nov — Tibesti: Fighting continued despite the Mediator of the Republic's call for a cessation of hostilities from 7 Nov. A military source told AFP on 28 Oct that at least 72 soldiers had been wounded since 14 Oct; overall tolls remain unverified.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The Miski conflict has moved into a phase of government drone strikes against a militia that still controls the town and blocks access to its gold deposits, and the mediator's call for a ceasefire from 7 November has not held. Chad also faces repeated lethal intercommunal violence (Koula, 25 dead on 30 Oct), spillover from the Sudan war in the east, and Boko Haram activity around Lake Chad. It is not raised to CRITICAL because the state still controls the wider territory and the Tibesti fighting remains confined to one mining area. Over the next 90 days, continued strikes on Miski are likely, but a full army takeover of the town remains unlikely given the government's apparent preference for containment and pressure. Dry-season transhumance is likely to bring further deadly farmer–herder clashes in the centre and east. Heavy confirmed losses in Tibesti, or repeated large cross-border strikes from Sudan, would justify CRITICAL. Refugee arrivals from Darfur will stay high, and may rise as the army advances in West Kordofan push civilians toward Darfur.

forecasts.statement: The Chadian army takes control of the town of Miski in Tibesti from the Miski Self-Defence Committee, by force or under a negotiated handover.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if AFP, Reuters, RFI or Crisis Group reports on or before 12 Feb 2027 that Chadian state forces control Miski town.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 13 Nov — Nouakchott/Mali border: An analysis by the Spanish Institute for Strategic Studies (IEEE) named Mauritania as the Maghreb country most directly exposed to the deterioration in Mali, citing the porous border, the terrorist threat and the hosting of about 290,000 Malian refugees in Hodh Chargui. It noted Mauritania has suffered no attack since 2011.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed incident was reported inside Mauritania this week; the risks come from border friction with Mali, the pressure of around 290,000–400,000 Malian refugees in Hodh Chargui, food insecurity among them, and migration flows. Elite army units hold military zones along the Mali border. Over the next 90 days, FAMa and Africa Corps operations and JNIM activity in western and central Mali are likely to push more refugees into Hodh Chargui and risk incidents involving Mauritanian herders, keeping relations with Bamako tense. Nouakchott will likely continue containment through diplomatic protests and precautionary measures. A JNIM attack inside Mauritania or an armed border clash would justify HIGH; neither is likely in this period.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 15 Nov — Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda LGA, Zamfara: About 30 bandits, allegedly loyal to Bello Wakkala, attacked a mosque, killing seven worshippers including an aide to Governor Dauda Lawal and abducting 15, according to Daily Trust. Police gave a lower toll of one dead and four abducted. A separate attack on a home in the town on 16 Nov killed a guard.

15 Nov — Zwagal, Jipal district, Mangu LGA, Plateau: Gunmen attacked the village at night; nine victims were buried in a mass grave, and two more men were killed in an ambush in Bokkos LGA, bringing the toll to at least 11 (The Sun). The village head said the attackers spoke Fulani.

12 Nov — Kerenoa, Marte LGA, Borno: Air strikes on a suspected ISWAP hideout reportedly killed at least ten fighters, including attendees of a commanders' meeting, according to military-sourced reports. Not independently verified.

16–17 Nov — Monguno and Arinna (South Lake Chad), Borno: Operation Hadin Kai said air strikes killed 21 ISWAP fighters, including named leaders, and injured ten. The claim is not independently verified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Bandit attacks in Zamfara now reach mosques and officials in urban Kaura Namoda, Plateau saw another mass-casualty night raid in Mangu, and the military continues an intensive air campaign against ISWAP in Borno. Over the next 90 days ISWAP is likely to keep up night raids on forward bases in Kukawa, Ngala, Marte, Monguno and the Lake Chad islands as dry-season mobility improves; a single attack on a military base killing ten or more soldiers is likely. The military will keep claiming high enemy tolls from air operations that are hard to verify, with a standing risk of civilian casualties. Bandit groups in Zamfara, Katsina and Sokoto are likely to keep carrying out mass killings and kidnappings and to target security forces, officials and party events as the election cycle advances. Farmer–herder and reprisal violence in Plateau and Benue is likely to continue.

events.place: Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda LGA, Zamfara
Zwagal, Jipal district, Mangu LGA, Plateau
Monguno and Arinna (South Lake Chad), Borno

forecasts.statement: ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters attack a military base or forward position in Borno or Yobe in a single attack that reportedly kills ten or more Nigerian soldiers.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, HumAngle, Premium Times or Daily Trust reports, on or before 12 Feb 2027, a single attack in Borno or Yobe in which at least ten soldiers were killed (military, security-source or credible local tolls count).

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: Summit diplomacy dominated the week, and China lowered its military pressure around it. Trump met Marcos in Manila on 18 November and played down South China Sea tensions, then flew to the APEC summit in Shenzhen. There he met Xi on 19 November ahead of the first Xi–Trump–Putin trilateral, whose outcomes were not yet reported at the time of writing. The ASEAN summit in the Philippines (15–17 November) ended without the promised South China Sea Code of Conduct. PLA air activity around Taiwan fell to 60 sorties in the week of 9–15 November, down from 111, and Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office called Taiwan 'a purely internal matter' on the eve of the trilateral. Taiwan's 28 November local elections and the post-APEC period are now the main windows for renewed pressure.

Bangladesh had the region's sharpest deterioration. Unrest over Sheikh Hasina's announced December return and the banned Awami League's 19 November 'lockdown' produced crude-bomb blasts and arson in at least 28 districts. At least four people were killed on 17–18 November, including BNP leaders in Faridpur and Narail and a bus worker burned to death in Pirojpur. Mobs torched a police station in Tungipara, arsonists set Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home in Chattogram on fire, and dozens of Grameen Bank branches were attacked. BGB troops were deployed and 565 people were arrested in Dhaka in 24 hours. Bangladesh is raised to HIGH.

Pakistan's two insurgencies stayed lethal and are becoming more technical. On 12 November a BLA Majeed Brigade vehicle-borne suicide attack hit an FC post in the Kanak area of Mastung. Police say it killed two civilians and three attackers, while the BLA claims 18 personnel. Two days later an armed quadcopter killed an army major and a havildar in Balochistan. ISPR says 74 militants have been killed in KP and Balochistan since 3 November, including 24 on 13–14 November. In Myanmar, regime airstrikes killed at least 12 displaced people at the Byar La camp in Ponnagyun, Rakhine, on 13 November and kept hitting villages in Mon State and Magway, while the Arakan Army vowed to take Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Manaung.

The Korean peninsula was quiet militarily. No North Korean launch or new MDL incident was found for 12–19 November. Kim Jong Un ignored Trump's public calls for a meeting in China, touring Samjiyon with his daughter, and on 18 November attacked 'wicked enemies'' naval activities at a naval university, while his envoy Jo Yong Won went to Moscow. Seoul asked Beijing on 13 November to help bring Pyongyang back to talks. In India, a 13 November ambush on the Imphal–Ukhrul road killed four Naga civilians and set off a Manipur-wide shutdown. In Kulgam (J&K), security forces killed the LeT commander described as the last known active local militant in Kashmir on 18 November.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 15–16 Nov — Samjiyon, Ryanggang: KCNA showed Kim Jong Un with his daughter Ju Ae touring the Samjiyon airport reconstruction, a tourist railway and a ski resort. He made no response to Trump's repeated public calls to meet him in China during the APEC summit (NBC, Euronews).

18 Nov — Kim Jong Suk Naval University, South Hamgyong: During two days of field guidance in South Hamgyong, Kim criticised the naval activities of 'wicked enemies' and said the university's primary duty is to train professional naval commanders (KCNA via NK News).
14 Nov — Moscow: Senior party secretary Jo Yong Won arrived in Moscow for talks with Dmitry Medvedev, days before the Xi–Trump–Putin meeting in Shenzhen (state media via NK News).
12–19 Nov — North Korea: No missile launch was found for the period. The last confirmed launch remains the 4 November salvo from Sondok.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The week brought no launches. Pyongyang ignored Trump's summit overtures around APEC, staged leader appearances and sent a senior envoy to Moscow, while Kim's attack on enemy 'naval activities' points toward the navy as a focus of coming tests. Over the next 90 days, a ballistic missile launch reported by the JCS remains likely, possibly timed to the end of APEC diplomacy, year-end party plenums or allied drills. Expect cruise-missile and naval weapons trials and announcements tied to deploying new warhead types. Cyber theft will continue to fund the programme. A Trump–Kim meeting within the window is unlikely given Pyongyang's preconditions, and Kim is likely to keep prioritising Moscow and Beijing. The main escalation paths are still a DMZ exchange of fire or launches toward the NLL. An ICBM or nuclear test remains a low-probability wildcard.

events.place: Kim Jong Suk Naval University, South Hamgyong

forecasts.statement: North Korea launches at least one ballistic missile that South Korea's JCS publicly reports.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the JCS (as reported by Yonhap, Reuters or AP) announces at least one North Korean ballistic missile launch between 2026-11-12 and 2026-12-31. Cruise-missile or artillery-only launches do not count.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 13 Nov — Byar La IDP camp, Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine: Regime fighter jets bombed a displacement camp northeast of Sittwe without warning, killing 12 people, including a five-year-old, and injuring 18, according to witnesses and a rescue service (AFP). BNI gave an early toll of at least eight.

15–16 Nov — Ye Township, Mon State (NMSP area): Regime aircraft dropped two bombs on Kyae Daik village on 16 Nov, killing two civilians and injuring 14. Overnight bombing of Hlan Chaung Wa village, including from a Y-12 aircraft, killed one more and injured three (m.CDM).

13–14 Nov — Myaing and Mindon townships, Magway: The Myaing PDF said two children were killed after two days of regime airstrikes and drone attacks. On 16 Nov a fighter-jet strike on two villages in Mindon Township killed one civilian (m.CDM).

13–14 Nov — Rakhine: On the third anniversary of renewed fighting, the Arakan Army vowed to capture the three remaining regime-held townships, Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Manaung (Mizzima). A resistance digest reported that the regime destroyed four bridges leading to besieged Kyaukphyu on 14 Nov. This is unverified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The regime's air campaign is killing displaced people and villagers on several fronts. AAPP counted 122 people killed by airstrikes between 1 October and 11 November, and this week brought the Ponnagyun camp strike and bombing in the NMSP area of Mon State, which had been relatively spared. Over the next 90 days, expect continued jet, gyrocopter and drone strikes on Rakhine, Sagaing, Magway and the southeast, along with clearance operations that displace thousands. The AA's declared push on Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Manaung will intensify. Kyaukphyu matters to China, and a full capture of Sittwe in the window remains unlikely given the junta's reinforced garrison and naval resupply. Spillover into Thailand around Myawaddy will recur, and no negotiated de-escalation is in sight.

events.place: Byar La IDP camp, Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine

forecasts.statement: The Arakan Army takes full control of Sittwe, the Rakhine State capital, with junta forces withdrawn or defeated.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, The Irrawaddy or DVB report by 2027-02-12 that the AA controls Sittwe town and the regime's regional command there has fallen or withdrawn. AA claims alone do not count.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 12 Nov — Kanak area, Mastung, Balochistan: A vehicle-borne suicide attack struck an FC post. Police said forces repelled it and killed three attackers. The blast killed two civilians, injured three FC personnel and damaged homes and a mosque. The BLA's Majeed Brigade claimed it and says 18 personnel died, which is unverified.

13–14 Nov — Balochistan and North Waziristan: ISPR said an armed-quadcopter attack on army patrol vehicles in Balochistan killed Maj. Omer Minhas Nasir and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan, and the BLA claimed a drone strike near Mastung. Two more soldiers died in North Waziristan operations that ISPR says killed 16 militants, while eight more militants were killed near Kolpur.

13–18 Nov — Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Police said they foiled an attack on the Kingar Pul checkpoint, killing four militants they described as 'Fitna al-Khawarij' (TTP). On 18 Nov security forces killed four more in an operation in the Gidar Camp area.
13 Nov — KP and Balochistan: The military said 74 militants had been killed in raids along the Afghan border since 3 Nov. Border clashes with the Afghan Taliban continue without a ceasefire.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Both insurgencies are active at once. In Balochistan the BLA is combining VBIEDs, armed quadcopters and highway blockades, and it claims 38 personnel killed in 44 operations in 15 days, a claim that runs well above official figures. In KP, attacks on police and checkpoints continue after the deadly Kohat ambush, while ISPR reports high militant death tolls. Over the next 90 days, expect frequent TTP attacks on police and FC posts in Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Kohat, Dera Ismail Khan and the former tribal districts. The BLA is likely to keep up drone and suicide attacks in Mastung, Kech, Nushki and Kharan and to disrupt rail and highway traffic. A Pakistani air or drone strike inside Afghanistan remains likely, especially after a mass-casualty attack, and would trigger another round of border fighting.

forecasts.statement: Pakistan carries out at least one airstrike or drone strike inside Afghan territory.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report by 2027-02-12 a Pakistani air or drone strike on Afghan territory, confirmed by Pakistan or reported by the Taliban government. Cross-border artillery or small-arms fire alone does not count.

countries.name: India
incidents: 13 Nov — New Heaven, Imphal–Ukhrul road (NH-202), Ukhrul district, Manipur: Suspected militants fired on two vehicles, killing four Naga civilians: a mother and son and two siblings. Police suspect Kuki militants, and a Kuki body in Ukhrul denied involvement. It was the fourth ambush on the Litan–New Heaven stretch.

Mid-Nov — Manipur: The Ukhrul killings triggered a statewide shutdown and confrontations between protesters and security forces. Tangkhul civil-society groups gave the state and central governments a three-day ultimatum to flush out Kuki armed groups from Naga areas, and security forces began search and cordon operations.

16 Nov — Laroo, Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir: An encounter killed LeT associate Umar Nisar Dar after LeT commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat escaped the cordon. Reports differ on whether one or two militants died.

18 Nov — Zangalpora, Devsar, Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir: Security forces killed LeT commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat, whom agencies described as the last known active local militant in Kashmir, days after the 11 Nov attack on a CRPF patrol.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Kuki–Naga violence in Manipur produced its deadliest single incident in weeks with the 13 November Ukhrul ambush, which followed the fatal shooting of a Kuki woman in Senapati the day before. The ultimatum and shutdown create a clear risk of reprisals. Over the next 90 days, expect retaliatory shootings and ambushes along NH-2 and NH-202 (Senapati, Kangpokpi, Ukhrul, Noney), road blockades, intra-Naga factional clashes and further security operations. A single attack killing five or more people is a realistic possibility. In J&K, the Kulgam operations have dismantled the local LeT cell, but Pakistani militants in the Doda–Kishtwar forests remain, so expect sporadic attacks on security forces as winter reduces infiltration. India–Pakistan friction remains rhetorical, and no LoC incident was found.

events.place: New Heaven, Imphal–Ukhrul road (NH-202), Ukhrul district, Manipur
Zangalpora, Devsar, Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir

forecasts.statement: A single armed attack, ambush or clash in Manipur kills at least five people.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, PTI or a major Indian national outlet (The Hindu, Indian Express, NDTV) reports, between 2026-11-20 and 2027-01-31, one incident in Manipur (one attack, ambush or gunfight at one location on one day) with at least five people killed, including militants.
