Separate incidents may not be combined.

countries.name: China
incidents: 18–19 Nov — Shenzhen: China hosted the APEC leaders' meeting. Trump arrived on 18 Nov and began talks with Xi on 19 Nov ahead of the first Xi–Trump–Putin trilateral meeting, which was expected to cover Iran, Ukraine and nuclear proliferation. Readouts were not yet available.

18 Nov — Beijing: The Taiwan Affairs Office said Taiwan is 'a purely internal' matter, a day before the trilateral, without saying whether it would be discussed. Trump said in Manila that Xi would raise it.

9–15 Nov — Around Taiwan: PLA air activity fell to 60 sorties (37 entering the ADIZ), down about 46% from the previous week's 111, with a 'joint combat readiness patrol' on 12 Nov (Taiwan Security Monitor), as the early-November 100-plus-ship surge wound down.
13 Nov — Beijing: Foreign Minister Wang Yi met South Korea's Cho Hyun. Seoul says China agreed to work toward bringing North Korea back to talks (Korea JoongAng Daily).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. China's own territory faces no armed threat. As expected, Beijing paired summit hosting with a drawdown in military pressure: Taiwan-area sorties halved after the early-November unannounced surge. Over the next 90 days, expect Beijing to use any Trump–Xi understandings to press Washington on Taiwan arms sales while keeping coercive tools in reserve. A renewed surge or a named encirclement exercise remains a realistic possibility after Taiwan's 28 November elections or in response to US arms sales. CCG 'law-enforcement patrols' at Kinmen, Scarborough and the Senkakus will continue. The main risk remains an unplanned collision or close intercept with Japanese, Philippine or US forces.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 9–15 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND recorded 60 PLA aircraft sorties (37 entering the ADIZ), down from 111 the week before, with median-line crossings on 10, 12, 13 and 15 Nov and 'joint air-sea training' (a joint combat readiness patrol) on 12 Nov (Taiwan Security Monitor).

12–14 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND tracked seven PLA aircraft, seven warships and two official ships in the 24 hours to 12 Nov, and 10 aircraft, eight warships and three official ships to 14 Nov, when four fighters crossed the median line. One count gave 184 aircraft and 141 naval vessel detections for the month to 14 Nov (Taiwan News).

18 Nov — Beijing / Shenzhen: Ahead of the Xi–Trump–Putin meeting, China's Taiwan Affairs Office called Taiwan 'a purely internal' matter. Trump said in Manila that he would not have to raise Taiwan because Xi would.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. PLA activity fell back to routine levels during the APEC week, but the drop reflects summit timing, not a reduced threat. The early-November surge showed that Beijing can mass 100-plus ships from three theatre commands without notice, and on 3 November it flew 49 aircraft sorties in a day, the highest single-day total this year. Over the next 90 days, the 28 November local elections and the post-summit period are the most likely windows for renewed pressure. A named PLA exercise remains a realistic possibility, and a single-day spike of 45 or more sorties is a realistic possibility. Expect continued CCG pressure on Kinmen and Pratas, cognitive and election-interference operations, and close attention in Taipei to any US–China language on Taiwan from Shenzhen.

forecasts.statement: The PLA Eastern Theater Command announces a named large-scale military exercise around Taiwan (in the style of Strait Thunder or Justice Mission).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by 2027-02-12, the PLA Eastern Theater Command or Chinese state media publicly announce a drill around Taiwan under a specific exercise name, as reported by Reuters, AP or Taiwan's MND. Unannounced surges and routine 'joint combat readiness patrols' do not count.

forecasts.statement: Taiwan's MND reports at least 45 PLA aircraft sorties around Taiwan in a single daily (24-hour) report.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if any MND daily 'PLA activities in the waters and airspace around Taiwan' release issued between 2026-11-20 and 2027-01-31 reports 45 or more PLA aircraft sorties, as published by the MND or reported by Focus Taiwan, Taipei Times, Reuters or AP.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 18 Nov — Manila: Trump met Marcos at Malacañang before flying to Shenzhen. He said the South China Sea confrontations with China 'will be taken care of' and that the US was expanding defence cooperation, but announced no new treaty commitment (DPA). A trade deal was announced without disclosed terms.

15–17 Nov — Philippines: The 49th ASEAN Summit hosted by Manila ended without concluding the South China Sea Code of Conduct, missing the 2026 deadline. Manila says 80% of the text is agreed, and talks pass to Singapore's chairmanship (CNBC, Asia Times).

16 Nov — Central Mindanao (Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Cotabato): Four separate ambushes by unidentified gunmen killed three people, including retired soldier Danny Lakim in Datu Odin Sinsuat, and wounded four, among them Barangay Tumbras captain Fatima Mokamad (Philstar).

19 Nov — West Philippine Sea: PCG spokesman Jay Tarriela said the situation was generally calm despite the continued presence of CCG, maritime militia and other Chinese vessels in the EEZ, with no significant harassment of Filipino vessels recently (Daily Tribune).
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The sea was calm during the summit season, but the underlying standoff at Scarborough is unchanged: a permanent CCG, militia and PLAN presence, an unidentified Chinese platform in the lagoon and PLA readiness patrols. Trump's non-committal remarks in Manila and the failed Code of Conduct deadline leave Manila with weaker deterrence than it sought. Over the next 90 days, the post-summit lull is likely to give way to renewed CCG blocking and water-cannon use against BFAR, PCG and resupply missions at Scarborough, Second Thomas and Sabina Shoals. Expect PLA intercepts of Philippine aircraft and more Philippine–Japanese–US cooperation at sea. In Mindanao, ambushes, clan feuds and Dawlah Islamiyah remnants keep violence at a steady low level in the BARMM. A fatal incident at sea would trigger Mutual Defense Treaty consultations.

events.place: Central Mindanao (Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, Cotabato)

forecasts.statement: China Coast Guard vessels fire water cannon at a Philippine government vessel (PCG, BFAR or Navy) in the South China Sea.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by 2027-02-12, the PCG, the AFP or the Philippine NSC report a CCG water-cannon use against a Philippine government vessel, as carried by Reuters, AP or Philippine national media.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 13 Nov — Beijing: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun asked Wang Yi to help bring Pyongyang back to the table, and Seoul says China agreed. Seoul also warned Washington and Beijing that a US–China–Russia meeting 'must not become a second Yalta' that recognises North Korea as a nuclear state (Korea JoongAng Daily).

18–19 Nov — Shenzhen: President Lee attended APEC, where a summit with Xi was scheduled. NK News reported that Xi backed Seoul's push for US–North Korea dialogue during the meeting, while the presidential office said the future of US–North Korea dialogue remained 'unknown territory'.

12–19 Nov — Inter-Korean border: No new North Korean missile launch, MDL crossing, warning-shot or loudspeaker incident was found for the period. The September DMZ mine-blast dispute remains unresolved.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The week was diplomatically busy and militarily quiet. Seoul is trying to steer US–China–Russia summitry toward dialogue with Pyongyang without legitimising North Korea's nuclear status, while Pyongyang ignores both Seoul and Washington. The underlying DMZ risks remain: North Korean fortification work across the MDL, the unresolved September mine blast and the loudspeaker threat. Over the next 90 days, North Korean SRBM or cruise-missile launches toward the East Sea remain likely, and new South Korean warning shots at North Korean troops crossing the MDL remain likely, although winter may slow the fortification work. Watch for live fire across the MDL, mine or drone incidents, launches toward the NLL, and Pyongyang's reaction to any US–China statement on the peninsula.

forecasts.statement: South Korean troops fire warning shots at North Korean soldiers crossing the Military Demarcation Line.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the JCS, as reported by Yonhap, Korea JoongAng Daily, Reuters or AP, confirms at least one new warning-shot incident against North Korean troops crossing the MDL between 2026-11-12 and 2027-01-31.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 18–19 Nov — Shenzhen: General Secretary and State President To Lam met Xi Jinping on the sidelines of APEC, and the two sides exchanged views on maritime issues while Code of Conduct talks remain unresolved (Asia Times).

15–17 Nov — ASEAN Summit, Philippines: The summit ended without concluding the South China Sea Code of Conduct, missing the 2026 deadline. Vietnam, a claimant state, faces continued Chinese construction in the Paracels and its own Spratly fortification drive, which Bloomberg links to a growing risk of a clash. No Vietnam–China maritime incident was found for 12–19 Nov.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There was again no kinetic or maritime incident. Hanoi used the To Lam–Xi meeting at APEC as a safety valve while the Code of Conduct deadline lapsed and both sides continue building in the Spratlys and Paracels. Over the next 90 days, expect Vietnam to keep hedging through defence diplomacy with India, Australia, the US and Japan, with the December Vietnam International Defence Expo as a showcase, while protecting party-to-party ties with Beijing. Watch for CCG harassment or detention of Vietnamese fishermen in the Paracels, Chinese protests over Spratly reclamation, and any Chinese military deployment to Ban Keun in Laos. A direct naval confrontation remains unlikely.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 11–12 Nov — Yonaguni–Taiwan gap: According to Japan's Joint Staff, a Chinese Y-9 electronic-intelligence aircraft and a suspected Chinese UAV flew from the East China Sea between Yonaguni and Taiwan into the Philippine Sea, prompting ASDF scrambles (Zona Militar, Seoul Economic Daily).

9 Nov (latest found) — Senkaku Islands: The 9 Nov entry of four CCG ships into territorial waters off Kuba Island remains the most recent one found. Defense News (16 Nov) describes Chinese naval and coast-guard presence near Japan as 'normalised' since the 2025 diplomatic crisis, with Senkaku deployments at 'very high levels'.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; watch for an upgrade. Chinese reconnaissance flights through the Yonaguni and Miyako gaps continued after the early-November naval surge, but no airspace violation, radar lock-on or missile impact in Japan's EEZ was found. Japan was largely a bystander to the Shenzhen summitry, while the China–Japan diplomatic freeze persists. Over the next 90 days, another CCG entry into Senkaku territorial waters is likely by year-end. Expect more PLAN and drone transits of the Ryukyu gaps, possible Chinese–Russian joint bomber flights, and North Korean launches into the Sea of Japan. A close-quarters air or maritime incident, a radar lock-on or a missile landing in Japan's EEZ would justify raising Japan to HIGH.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 13 Nov — Dekai, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: A wood cutter was allegedly killed in an attack that police attribute to a TPNPB-OPM ('KKB') group. Damai Cartenz personnel said they came under fire on the way to the scene, and police are pursuing suspects (Kompas, Tribunnews).
14 Nov — Oksibil, Pegunungan Bintang: The Damai Cartenz task force ran patrols on suspected armed-group crossing routes after the latest Yahukimo incidents.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Reporting from Papua remains sparse, and a lack of reports is not calm. Yahukimo has had a firefight and camp seizure (7–8 November), a fatal attack on a civilian worker (13 November) and repeated shootings since September. The TPNPB claimed attacks on road workers and a security convoy in Tambrauw on 4–5 November. Over the next 90 days, expect continued TNI and police operations (Habema, Damai Cartenz) in Yahukimo, Nduga, Intan Jaya, Puncak, Maybrat and Tambrauw, with disputed casualty claims and displacement. TPNPB attacks on road workers, miners, aviation and alleged informants are likely to continue, with heightened risk around the 1 December 'national day'. Jakarta shows no sign of opening dialogue.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 10–11 Nov — Yala, Songkhla and Satun: In coordinated insurgent attacks on 13 sites, about 20 armed, masked men tied up five guards and bombed and burned the Yala subdistrict administrative organisation office and official vehicles in Mueang Yala. Other strikes hit five Yala districts, utility poles in Sadao and Chana (Songkhla) and a checkpoint in Thung Wa (Satun), where three students in a van were slightly hurt. ISOC Region 4 condemned the attacks (Thai PBS World).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The coordinated 13-site wave on 10–11 November came a day after security forces killed the Lam Phaya attack suspect in Yala. It reached Satun, normally outside the core conflict zone, and shows that insurgent networks can still synchronise attacks across provinces, though casualties were light. No new incident was found for 12–19 November, and no new shelling from Myanmar into Tak. Over the next 90 days, expect sporadic IEDs, arson and ambushes in Narathiwat, Pattani, Yala and the Songkhla border districts, possible reprisals for the 9 November killing, and continued security sweeps near the Malaysian border. Myanmar's fighting around Myawaddy will keep sending shells and refugees into Tak. A mass-casualty coordinated attack would warrant reassessment.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 17 Nov — Faridpur and Gopalganj: A BNP activist was killed during a protest near Hasina's home district of Gopalganj (Reuters, police). Other reports name a BNP leader killed in Faridpur amid BNP–Awami League clashes, and a BNP lawmaker's house and BNP supporters' shops in Gopalganj were set on fire. The same night a crude bomb exploded outside Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury's residence in Dhaka.

18 Nov — Pirojpur and Tungipara (Gopalganj): Arsonists set two buses on fire in Pirojpur, burning a bus company helper to death. A mob torched a police station and police vehicles in Tungipara, Hasina's hometown, after clashes with Awami League activists (Reuters).
18–19 Nov — Narail: Two local BNP leaders were killed when Awami League activists attacked a BNP march (PTI via ThePrint).

19 Nov — Dhaka and Chattogram: The banned Awami League's nationwide 'lockdown', on the anniversary of Hasina's death sentence, opened with pre-dawn crude-bomb blasts in Dhaka. Arsonists set Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home in Panchlaish, Chattogram, on fire, and at least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices have been targeted since 10 Nov. Police arrested 565 people in Dhaka in 24 hours, and BGB troops were deployed in sensitive districts.
countries.coa: HIGH raised from MODERATE. Hasina's announced December return and the government's refusal to issue her documents have turned the banned Awami League's protest campaign into nationwide violent unrest. Its features are crude bombs and vehicle arson in 28 districts, targeted killings of BNP figures, attacks on police stations, ministers' homes and Yunus-linked property, and tit-for-tat arson against Awami League leaders' homes. The state is responding with mass arrests and BGB deployments. Over the next 90 days, expect recurring hartal and lockdown calls, crude-bomb attacks and arson, BNP–Awami League clashes centred on Gopalganj, Faridpur, Narail and Dhaka, and harsher crackdowns that risk deaths from police fire. A day with five or more deaths in this violence is a realistic possibility. An actual Hasina return, which would mean arrest under her death sentence, is unlikely, but the build-up to December will itself drive unrest. Garment-wage protests in Gazipur and Ashulia add a second flashpoint. Lowering back to MODERATE would require the Awami League campaign to subside without further killings.

forecasts.statement: Political violence linked to the Awami League protest campaign (clashes, bombings, arson or police fire) kills at least five people in Bangladesh on a single day.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, The Daily Star or Prothom Alo report, between 2026-11-20 and 2027-01-31, at least five deaths on one calendar day nationwide in clashes, attacks, arson or security-force fire connected to Awami League protests, lockdowns or Hasina's return, or to reprisals against them.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 2 Nov — Kappalthurai, Uppuveli, Trincomalee: A gunman with a suspected T-56 rifle fired on a hired three-wheeler, killing a 39-year-old man (identified as a Navy sailor) and wounding two. Police suspect a drug-trafficking dispute.
8 Nov (report) — Trincomalee: Police said three suspects, including the alleged gunman, a legally discharged former army soldier arrested in Dikwella on 6 Nov, were in custody (Newswire, Ada Derana).
countries.coa: LOW maintained. No new security incident was found for 12–19 November. The violence picture remains criminal: underworld and narcotics-linked shootings, often by ex-military gunmen, plus police shootouts and custodial-death controversies such as the 3 November Bogambara prison shooting. No insurgent, terrorist or communal violence was found. Over the next 90 days, expect continued gang shootings in the Western, Southern and Eastern provinces and arrests under the anti-drug drive, with no change in the overall threat picture.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Haiti: El Salvador's decapitation campaign widened and became more openly unilateral. On 18 November, Salvadoran helicopters destroyed the Canaan mansion of Taliban gang leader Jeff Larose ('Jeff Canaan'), a day after thousands of Haitians marched in support of Bukele. The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force said it was not involved, and it is unclear whether Larose was inside. ACLED counts more than 100 killed during the Salvadoran intervention as of 11 November, at least 26 of them civilians. Reuters reports about 7,000 people have fled the area where the four Salvadoran soldiers went missing on 18 October; they are still unaccounted for. Haiti's justice minister says there is 'no date' for the Salvadorans to leave.

Colombia: the action-reaction cycle tightened. An ELN-attributed explosive-drone attack killed four soldiers in rural Tibu (Catatumbo) on 12 November, the second deadly drone attack on troops in a week. De la Espriella promised 'for every attack, a bombing' and a counter-drone plan covering 16 departments. El Tiempo now counts nine bombings in 100 days of government, including the 10 November 'Operation Nehemias' against the Clan del Golfo in Taraza (Antioquia), which killed 10 according to the Defence Ministry. Across the border, Venezuela's FANB launched 'Operation Sovereignty and Peace' in three Apure municipalities on 12 November, targeting irregular camps and airstrips after the ELN seized a Colombian second lieutenant.

Ecuador and Peru: emergency measures are not suppressing criminal violence. Noboa renewed the state of exception in eight provinces for 30 days on 11 November (Decree 532), with no curfew, ahead of the 29 November local elections. At least 27 people were killed on 15–17 November, including five in one shooting in Machala and three at a nightclub in Playas, among them a police sergeant. In Peru, a Los Mandarinos bus driver was shot dead in Jicamarca on 17 November and the company stopped work, while cargo hauliers blocked highways in a 72-hour national strike over diesel prices on 16–18 November.

Elsewhere, the pressure is political and humanitarian. Venezuela opened a fourth round of government–opposition talks in Caracas on 13 November, covering the Supreme Court, the CNE and Machado's disqualification, though Machado is not at the table. Foro Penal counts 321 political prisoners, and Daniel Echenagucia was released on 14 November. In Cuba, the generation deficit stayed around 1,700–1,900 MW, Havana's Calabazar saw a blackout protest with burning barricades on 13 November, and historian Alina Barbara Lopez was detained in Matanzas on 18 November. In Bolivia, cocaleros ambushed an anti-drug police patrol in Villa Tunari on 11 November and retook the El Castillo checkpoint, and a migration alert now bars Morales from leaving the country. The Dominican border stays calm under a heavy military presence. Jamaica's violence remains criminal, with continued fatal police shootings in St Catherine.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 12 Nov — Apure state: The FANB strategic command (CEOFANB) announced a military deployment, reported as 'Operation Sovereignty and Peace', in three Apure municipalities to dismantle irregular-group logistics camps and clandestine airstrips. It follows the ELN Eastern War Front's 5 November confirmation that it holds a Colombian army second lieutenant seized in Arauca; official statements do not name the ELN.

13 Nov — Caracas: The Rodriguez government and the opposition delegation of the 2015 National Assembly opened a fourth round of talks at the Gran Melia hotel, behind closed doors and with US backing. The agenda covers renewal of the Supreme Court, restructuring of the CNE and the law used to disqualify Maria Corina Machado, who is not taking part.

14 Nov — Caracas: The government's Programme for Peace and Democratic Coexistence confirmed the release under precautionary measures of Italian-Venezuelan political prisoner Daniel Echenagucia, who then left the country. Foro Penal's latest count (to 9 November) is 321 political prisoners: 171 awaiting judgment and 150 convicted.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Inside Venezuela, the week brought no clashes with protesters, no mass arrests and no reported casualties. The political contest moved into a fourth negotiating round on the Supreme Court, the CNE and Machado's disqualification, and drip-feed prisoner releases continue: Foro Penal still counts 321 political prisoners. The new security element is the FANB's announced Apure deployment against irregular camps and airstrips after the ELN seized a Colombian officer, two weeks after the US-supported 30 October strike on an ELN camp. So far it is a state-initiated operation with no reported fighting or casualties, so it does not meet the HIGH threshold. Over the next 90 days, expect the talks to produce partial institutional deals (new Supreme Court or CNE appointments, possible reform of the disqualification law) before any election date, and more releases timed to the negotiations. In Apure, Zulia and Tachira, expect continued FANB pressure on ELN and dissident structures, increasingly coordinated with Bogota and Washington. An armed ELN response that kills Venezuelan troops is unlikely but is the main escalation path. Upgrade to HIGH if FANB–ELN fighting becomes recurrent with casualties, if strikes become regular, or if Machado is detained or rallies are dispersed with deaths.

forecasts.statement: Venezuela's interim government or the CNE officially announces a specific date for a presidential election.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or EFE report that the Rodriguez government or the National Electoral Council has formally set a calendar date for a presidential election by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: At least one member of Venezuela's armed forces (FANB) is killed in an armed clash with or attack by the ELN or FARC dissidents on Venezuelan territory.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE, Efecto Cocuyo, El Pitazo or the FANB itself report that at least one Venezuelan soldier or National Guard member was killed by the ELN or a FARC dissident group inside Venezuela between 19 November 2026 and 15 February 2027.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 12 Nov — Tibu, Norte de Santander (vereda Barco La Silla): Explosives dropped from drones killed four soldiers of Land Operations Battalion No. 10 and wounded two to five more. Military sources point to the ELN, though other armed groups operate in the area. President De la Espriella vowed 'they will pay' and ordered a full Public Force deployment.

10 Nov (disclosed by 15 Nov) — Taraza, Antioquia: The bombing announced on 10 November was 'Operation Nehemias' against the Clan del Golfo. The Defence Ministry reported 10 dead, while La FM reported eight members of the Manuel Alexander Ariza Gutierrez substructure killed. El Tiempo counts nine government bombings in its first 100 days, after the military acknowledged an unreported October strike in Cumaribo, Vichada.

16 Nov — Sardinata, Norte de Santander (San Martin de Loba): Drones dropped explosives on several points of the village, reportedly including health and education facilities, and residents fled. The ELN's Northeastern War Front blamed FARC dissident Front 33. No casualties had been reported by 18 November.

16 Nov — National: The government outlined a counter-drone emergency plan covering 16 of 32 departments. The FIP has recorded 318 explosive-drone attacks between January and 1 October 2026, about 72% attributed to EMC dissidents and 23% to the ELN.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Armed groups killed four more soldiers with explosive drones in Tibu on 12 November, the third deadly drone attack on troops in about ten days after San Jose del Palmar and Santa Rosa del Sur. The ELN and Front 33 are using drones against each other and against civilians in Catatumbo. The state's air campaign has reached nine bombings in 100 days, the latest killing about 10 Clan del Golfo members in Taraza. With ongoing hostilities, weekly deaths and armed-group control of parts of Catatumbo, Cauca, Choco and southern Bolivar, the CRITICAL definition is clearly met. Over the next 90 days, expect De la Espriella's 'for every attack, a bombing' line to sustain or raise the pace of air strikes, increasingly against the ELN in Catatumbo and Arauca, with US intelligence support and closer coordination with Venezuela's FANB along the Apure border. Expect continued drone and explosive retaliation against bases, police stations and toll booths. The counter-drone plan will take months to show effect. A single attack killing five or more security-force members remains a realistic possibility; the Tibu attack, with four dead, came close. Also watch for civilian deaths in bombings, which would draw legal and political challenges.

forecasts.statement: A single attack by an armed group in Colombia kills five or more soldiers and/or police officers.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE or Colombian national media (El Tiempo, El Espectador) report one incident (one attack or ambush on one day) in which at least five members of the security forces were killed by an armed group, by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: The Colombian government carries out at least four new aerial bombing operations against armed groups after 15 November 2026 (El Tiempo counted nine under President De la Espriella by that date).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the President, the Defence Ministry or the Military Forces announce or acknowledge at least four new aerial bombing operations conducted between 16 November 2026 and 15 February 2027, as reported by El Tiempo, El Espectador, Infobae or EFE.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 18 Nov — Canaan, north of Port-au-Prince: President Bukele said Salvadoran troops demolished the mansion of Taliban gang leader Jeff Larose ('Jeff Canaan'), releasing video of helicopters firing on it. It is unclear whether Larose was inside or killed. The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force said it was not involved, and Haitian police participation is unclear.

17 Nov — Port-au-Prince and other towns: Thousands of Haitians marched in support of Bukele and the Salvadoran troops. Haiti's justice minister said there is 'no date' for the Salvadoran forces to leave, as they are needed to back the police until elections next year.

17 Nov — Port-au-Prince area: Reuters, citing the UN, reported that some 7,000 people have fled their homes around the area where the four Salvadoran soldiers went missing on 18 October; they remain unaccounted for. A separate report warned that more than 250,000 Haitian children are at risk of acute malnutrition as violence blocks aid.

To 11 Nov — Haiti: ACLED counts more than 100 people killed during El Salvador's intervention, at least 26 of them civilians. Al Jazeera and AP put the toll of the 8 November strike on 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph's compound at about 20. Joseph, who survived, had asked the UN for talks, but the government insists any dialogue follow its own roadmap.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Gangs still control most of Port-au-Prince and the main roads north and east, and they hold four Salvadoran soldiers. Foreign and Haitian forces are striking gang leaders' homes and strongholds by helicopter and drone, with ACLED counting more than 100 dead, at least 26 of them civilians. That is active armed conflict with loss of state control over a significant part of the territory. The campaign is now extending from 400 Mawozo to other Viv Ansanm leaders. Jeff Larose of the Taliban gang (Canaan) was targeted on 18 November in an operation the GSF says it was not part of, which deepens the parallel-command problem. Popular backing for Bukele is visible in the street, and the government is rejecting talks outside its roadmap, so Joseph's talks offer has gone nowhere. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Salvadoran strikes on gang leaders around Croix-des-Bouquets, Canaan and Cite Soleil, gang reprisals against civilians and more displacement, as about 7,000 have already fled around the area where the soldiers went missing. Expect also mounting UN and NGO scrutiny of civilian harm. The capture or death of a top-tier leader (Joseph, Larose or Cherizier) is a realistic possibility. The missing soldiers' fate remains the main escalation trigger. Watch also whether the December electoral timetable slips because of the fighting.

forecasts.statement: 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph ('Lanmo Sanjou') is killed or taken into custody.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Haitian authorities, the Salvadoran government or the GSF confirm Joseph's death, capture or surrender, as reported by AP, Reuters, the Miami Herald or the Haitian Times, by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: Haitian or Salvadoran authorities confirm the fate (found alive or confirmed dead) of the four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing since 18 October.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Salvadoran or Haitian government officially states that the four technicians have been recovered alive or that their deaths are confirmed (identified remains included), as reported by AP, Reuters or Al Jazeera, by 31 January 2027.

forecasts.statement: Taliban gang leader Jeff Larose ('Jeff Canaan') is killed or taken into custody.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Haitian authorities, the Salvadoran government or the GSF confirm Larose's death, capture or surrender, as reported by AP, Reuters, the Miami Herald or the Haitian Times, by 15 February 2027.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 13 Nov — Calabazar and Las Canas, Boyeros (Havana): Dozens of residents, many of them young, blocked a bridge, set fire to rubbish and tyres, banged pots and chanted 'We want light!' after days with only one or two hours of electricity and water shortages. Police and officers put out the fire, power was restored shortly afterwards, and no arrests were reported (14ymedio).

15 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union forecast availability of 970 MW against peak demand of 2,800 MW, a deficit of about 1,830 MW. The actual peak shortfall reached 1,878 MW on 14 November and 1,735 MW on 17 November.

18 Nov — Matanzas: Historian Alina Barbara Lopez was detained outside the Provincial Court before a peaceful protest demanding a date for her long-suspended trial. The Cuban Observatory for Freedom of Expression says she has been detained several times this year when attempting her monthly protests.

17 Nov — Havana: Ladies in White leader Berta Soler was questioned over a 7 November protest about water shortages in Lawton and warned that blocking a public road to protest is a crime. Food-aid organiser Yoel Perez Serrano, detained on 7 November in El Cobre, has not been reported released.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Basic services remain in collapse: peak generation covers only about a third of demand, with daily shortfalls of 1,700–1,900 MW, and water supply is failing in parts of Havana. Unrest keeps flaring locally, most recently with barricades and pot-banging in Calabazar on 13 November. The state answers with targeted detentions and warnings to activists (Alina Barbara Lopez, Berta Soler, Perez Serrano) rather than lethal force, which fits HIGH rather than CRITICAL. Over the next 90 days, expect continued 1,700+ MW deficits, at least one further total or partial collapse of the national grid (a total disconnection remains likely), and recurring pot-banging and road-blocking protests in Havana's outer municipalities and the eastern provinces. Expect these to be met with short detentions, fines under Decree-Law 370 and localised internet cuts. Upgrade to CRITICAL only if protests coordinate across several cities, security forces use lethal force, or state control visibly erodes.

forecasts.statement: Cuba's national electric system (SEN) suffers a total nationwide disconnection (complete grid collapse).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Ministry of Energy and Mines or the UNE announces a total disconnection of the SEN, as reported by EFE, Reuters, AP or 14ymedio, by 12 February 2027. Partial or regional collapses do not count.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 11 Nov — Guayas, Manabi, El Oro, Los Rios, Esmeraldas, Pichincha, Santa Elena, Santo Domingo: President Noboa signed Executive Decree 532, renewing the state of exception for 'grave internal commotion' for 30 days (to about 13 December), without a curfew. The decree cited 322 intentional homicides in these provinces between 14 October and 1 November, 144 of them in Guayas, and the 29 November local elections.
15 Nov — Machala, El Oro: A gunman on a motorcycle opened fire on a group of friends in the 24 de Septiembre neighbourhood, killing five people and wounding four.
15 Nov — Playas (General Villamil), Guayas: Gunmen attacked a birthday party at a nightclub, killing three people, including an active-duty police sergeant, and wounding six.

15–17 Nov — Manabi, Guayas, El Oro, Santa Elena: La Republica counted at least 27 violent deaths in three days, including six killings in under 12 hours in the Manta–Montecristi area on 15 November and three more in Guayaquil the same afternoon. Police report 7,026 violent deaths nationally from 1 January to 9 November, 11.5% fewer than in 2025.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Days after the curfew ended on 10 November, the country again recorded massacre-style shootings in Machala and Playas, with a police sergeant among the dead, and at least 27 killings in 72 hours. The election campaign has also turned lethal: Huaquillas mayoral candidate Ronald Farfan was reportedly killed with a council candidate on 9 November. The government has renewed the 'grave internal commotion' state of exception in eight provinces without a curfew. National homicides are down about 11% year on year but remain around 22 a day, so large-scale organised violence with regular deaths continues. Over the next 90 days, the 29 November local elections are the main near-term risk, with further attacks on candidates, officials and journalists plausible in El Oro, Manabi, Guayas and Los Rios. After the vote, expect renewal of the state of exception around 13 December, continued military-police sweeps against Los Lobos, Los Choneros and Los Lagartos, prison violence, and a fifth curfew if killings spike, which remains likely.

forecasts.statement: President Noboa decrees a fifth curfew of 2026–27 covering at least one coastal province (Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro or Esmeraldas).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if an executive decree imposing a new night-time curfew in at least one of these provinces takes effect after 12 November 2026, as reported by Primicias, El Universo, EFE or Reuters, by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 17 Nov — Jicamarca, San Juan de Lurigancho (Lima): Gunmen posing as passengers shot dead Los Mandarinos bus driver Jose Miranda more than five times. The company says it pays about S/259 a day in extortion to the Los Chukis gang and suspects a rival group. More than 200 workers stopped work on 18 November and planned a march to the Interior Ministry.

16–18 Nov — Ancash, Huanuco and other regions: Heavy-cargo hauliers held a 72-hour national strike over diesel prices, blocking roads in Casma and other points, with the largest concentration in Huanuco. Organisers claimed about 20,000 participants, though some unions, including Arequipa truckers, stayed out.

12–14 Nov — Piura, Lima, Callao, Junin: La Republica reported four people killed in less than 48 hours in separate attacks. The Public Ministry counted 164 attacks on transport workers (93 dead, 124 wounded) from January to 27 October 2026.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Extortion gangs keep killing transport workers in Lima. The 17 November killing of a Los Mandarinos driver in Jicamarca, reportedly the fifth worker that company has lost, came a week after the 10 November anti-extortion march. Hauliers have meanwhile shown they can block highways for three days over fuel prices. This is recurring lethal violence by organised criminal groups plus disruptive social protest, while the state retains territorial control, which fits HIGH. Transport unions have conditioned a full stoppage on government action. Interior Minister Astudillo's weekly meetings have not stopped the killings, and unions call the government 'indifferent'. Over the next 90 days, expect continued driver and mototaxi killings, company-level stoppages after each killing, and a likely citywide public-transport strike in Lima/Callao. Expect also more emergency extensions and arrests of extortion cells, and renewed cargo blockades if the diesel dispute is not settled. Upgrade triggers: a mass-casualty attack on a bus, attacks on officials, or deadly clashes during strikes or road blockades.

forecasts.statement: Public transport unions in Lima/Callao carry out a strike (paro) against extortion in which a majority of formal bus companies suspend service for at least one day.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Peruvian national media (El Comercio, La Republica, RPP, Infobae Peru) or Reuters/AP report a transport strike in Lima/Callao described as widespread or as paralysing most routes, held after 12 November 2026 and by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 11 Nov — El Castillo checkpoint, Villa Tunari (Chapare): Cocaleros clashed with an anti-drug UMOPAR patrol at dawn. Accounts differ on whether it was an ambush during the anti-drug 'Operation Muralla' or a reaction to police breaking up a vigil. Three officers, including UMOPAR's national commander, were wounded and a police post was burned; police withdrew to Chimore, residents retook the checkpoint, and Morales praised them. No arrests were reported.

12–13 Nov — La Paz/Cochabamba: The government blamed Evo Morales for the El Castillo clash, and police announced reinforcements in the Tropico and prosecutions for the damage. Prosecutors have opened an 'armed uprising' and terrorism investigation in which Morales calls the Government Minister a narco in return.

13 Nov (reported 16 Nov) — National: At the prosecution's request, the Migration directorate issued an alert barring Morales from leaving Bolivia in the 'armed uprising' case over the 53-day May–June blockade. The case also names COB leader Mario Argollo and Tupac Katari federation leader Vicente Salazar, who is already jailed.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The El Castillo clash is the first violent confrontation in the Chapare in weeks: three police were wounded, and Morales loyalists forced police out of a checkpoint and now hold it. There were no deaths, though, and outside the Tropico the country saw no blockades or clashes, so the situation remains localised unrest with limited violence. The trend is toward confrontation. The government is pursuing an 'armed uprising' case, has added a migration alert and is reinforcing police in the Tropico, while Morales loyalists say they will block any operation against him. Over the next 90 days, expect further friction around anti-drug operations in the Chapare, intermittent contained blockades, COB pressure over fuel prices, and renewal of the state of exception that expires around 17 December. A police or military operation to arrest Morales is unlikely in the short term but would be the main escalation trigger. Upgrade to HIGH if such an operation meets armed resistance, if clashes in the Tropico cause deaths, or if multi-day blockades of main highways resume.

forecasts.statement: Bolivian police or armed forces launch an operation inside the Tropico de Cochabamba (Chapare) aimed at arresting Evo Morales.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE or Bolivian national media (El Deber, Los Tiempos, Pagina Siete) report that security forces moved into the Chapare in an attempt to execute an arrest warrant against Morales, whether or not the arrest succeeds, by 15 February 2027.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 12 Nov — Jimani: An EFE report from the border found crossings operating normally under a heavy military presence, with General Soto Thorman saying the frontier is 'secure and under Dominican control'. About 11,000 troops are deployed from Montecristi to Pedernales, reinforced since late October by special-forces battalions, armoured vehicles and drones.

16 Nov — Border: EFE reported the border fence, under construction for five years, gaining renewed priority because of Haiti's gang violence. When complete it will cover 160 km of the 391-km land border. President Abinader has said gangs will not be allowed to establish themselves within 20 km of the frontier.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. There was no organised armed or political violence on Dominican territory, and border crossings operate normally under a defensive build-up of about 11,000 troops. Over the next 90 days, Salvadoran strikes on gang leaders north and east of Port-au-Prince (Canaan, Croix-des-Bouquets) and the resulting displacement are the main external risk. They could push fleeing gang members or civilians toward Jimani and Belladere. Santo Domingo's declared intelligence and logistics support to El Salvador could also make Dominican interests a target for Viv Ansanm. Expect continued reinforcements, fence construction, mass deportations and possible temporary crossing closures if fighting moves east. Upgrade to MODERATE if gang fighting crosses the border, Dominican forces engage armed groups, or cross-border incidents cause casualties.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 11–12 Nov — Ellerslie Pen, Spanish Town (St Catherine): A police-military team fatally shot 23-year-old security guard Shevon Ulett during a search. Police say he fired at them first.
14 Nov — Portmore (St Catherine): Police fatally shot a man known as 'Topey' who they say attacked officers with a machete after an earlier dispute. INDECOM has opened a probe.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Violence remains individual criminal shootings and contested police killings, not organised political or armed-group violence. National murder figures remain on track for a historic low. The main concern is still the high rate of fatal police shootings: two more in St Catherine this week, after at least five in the south-central parishes in the preceding ten days, all subject to INDECOM probes. Over the next 90 days, expect further contested police shootings, roadblock protests after disputed killings, and the usual December rise in criminal violence. Upgrade to MODERATE only if planned ambushes on police, sustained unrest in Kingston, St Andrew or St Catherine, or a sharp rise in gang feuds emerges.
